sentences.text: Hundreds of members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and eunuchs from the East Depot gathered in one place would have been quite a sight on its own.
But not as much as the expressions on their faces right now.
Shock.
Astonishment.
Confusion.
Anger.
Those emotions swept across the countless faces surrounding us.
Every last one of them stared wide-eyed, gaped in disbelief, wondered if they’d heard right, and then, once reality sank in, used every muscle in their faces to express their fury.
Except for two people.
“...Young Master Jin?”
Hong Jin looked at me with dazed eyes.
“Ha.
Fuck.
I’m screwed again...”
Hyuk Mujin dragged a hand down his face with a deep sigh.
Hmm.
Hong Jin was one thing, but Hyuk Mujin had suffered because of me more than once or twice.
I did feel a little bad for him.
Still...
So what?
He could be squad leader, then.
Besides, this was a royal decree from His Highness Prince Shangshan himself.
As a citizen of Korea—no, of the Great Nation—I had no choice but to follow it wholeheartedly.
Of course, I’d never even seen an identity tag bearing my name, and I had no intention of getting one.
But anyway, that was the idea.
In short, this was a legally sanctioned rampage.
“I answered honestly, just as you ordered.
I’m not sure whether my answer pleased you, Your Highness.”
At my casual remark, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao, who’d been staring at me with round eyes, flashed a mischievous grin.
“No.
That was exactly the honest answer I wanted.
Though I was a little surprised.”
A little?
He’d looked pretty damn surprised.
Even that young prince, who’d shown such unexpected boldness, seemed taken aback by just how far I’d gone.
But I didn’t particularly regret it.
Whether we were in Murim or the imperial palace, this was a world where showing weakness meant getting devoured.
A rat cornered in an alley and cowering wouldn’t survive long.
A cat would bat it around like a toy until it finally stopped breathing.
If we have to stand up to them anyway, showing our teeth might buy us more time.
I hadn’t charged in without thinking, either.
The Son of Heaven had brought Prince Shangshan all the way to the Imperial Capital.
That meant he intended to get rid of him only after establishing some kind of pretext.
And that meant the hunting dogs snarling at us from every direction would stay docile until their master gave the order.
Even the pack leader with the sharpest teeth.
“Well.
I hardly know what to say.”
Was Baek Yeon so composed because he commanded so many members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard?
Or because he was a master who’d already reached the realm of the superhuman?
Whatever the reason, his reaction was different.
He didn’t show the near-killing-intent fury of the others, or toy with his weapon as though killing me were his lifelong wish.
He merely stroked his beard and said, “A word of advice: watch your tongue next time.
This is the imperial court of the Great Nation, not Murim.”
I scratched my chin.
“I did what His Highness told me to, and now I’m getting scolded for it.
How’s a powerless commoner like me supposed to live with that?”
I shot a sidelong glance at the prince.
He caught the signal and spoke up.
“Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
This man merely followed my orders.
You will say no more about it.”
Baek Yeon didn’t answer.
As he looked down at the prince with an inscrutable gaze, Zhu Bao’s voice grew firmer.
“I am asking you.
Why do you not answer?”
Ah.
I couldn’t let that go.
“That’s right!
How dare you ignore His Highness?
You insolent bastard!”
Good projection.
Good timing.
Fwoooosh.
And what an atmosphere.
My stern rebuke landed with a satisfying three-quarter beat.
Energy seethed all around us.
Hong Jin let out a quiet groan.
Hyuk Mujin grabbed my sleeve and whispered frantically, “Captain.
Captain.
Please, stop.”
“His Highness Prince Shangshan, the younger brother of His Majesty the Emperor, is asking you a question!
If you don’t answer, that’s an insult to the imperial family!
You’re a traitor!”
“Have you actually lost your mind?
Have you been dragging me around all this time just to get me killed in a place like this?”
“Let go of me, you pathetic fool who can’t even use Sword Energy!
Are you on their side, too?”
“No, fuck.
Please...”
Just as Hyuk Mujin was starting to sound half in tears, Baek Yeon, who’d been staring silently at Prince Shangshan the whole time, raised one hand.
Swish.
The oppressive air scattered in an instant.
The members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, furious at the insult to their superior, withdrew their auras as one.
Baek Yeon opened his firmly shut lips.
“Please forgive me, Your Highness.
I am slow-witted, and hesitated because I did not know how to answer.”
Not a single person here would be fool enough to take that at face value.
Not even a young prince who knew nothing of the world.
“I forgive you.
But having hesitated, you had better give the right answer.”
Watching Zhu Bao respond with such dignity, I realized something anew.
Regardless of his age, he was a member of the imperial family, born to noble blood.
Someone destined to become a dragon if only he could obtain the dragon pearl.
Perhaps even Hong Jin, who’d stood by Prince Shangshan for so many years, had underestimated him.
Perhaps so had the all-powerful man who remembered only the child who’d barely survived countless purges and been forced to leave for Shanxi Province with the one eunuch still at his side.
“I, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, will engrave Your Highness’s command deep in my heart.”
Clank.
At the scrape of golden armor, I saw Prince Shangshan’s shoulders twitch.
He had a boldness and dignity beyond his years, but he was still a child.
Facing one of the most powerful men in the Imperial Capital must have taken more courage than I’d imagined.
In that case...
A little help wouldn’t hurt.
Swish.
I murmured inwardly and, with all due insolence, brushed a hand against Prince Shangshan’s back.
The young prince looked up at me, eyes wide at the sudden warmth flowing into him.
Then he gave a faint smile and continued.
“These people are citizens of Shanxi Province, which I govern, and guests whom I personally invited.
There must be no neglect or mishap of any kind.
Is that understood?”
Baek Yeon glanced at me when he heard the prince’s newly clear voice, then replied with an odd expression.
“This is the imperial palace, where His Majesty the Emperor resides.
Who would dare harm Your Highness’s guests?”
I muttered as if to myself, “Who knows?
Someone’s already drawn a sword in front of His Highness.
What wouldn’t they do?”
“Good grief.
The world’s a frightening place these days, isn’t it, Your Highness?”
At my show of distress, Prince Shangshan looked at Baek Yeon once more.
“I believe he is right.
What do you think?”
A top tip for dealing with the imperial palace:
Get on good terms with a prince, and even the Emperor’s right-hand man can’t easily touch you—for now.
Just as I’d expected, Baek Yeon fell silent for a moment before giving the answer that had practically been decided already.
“I, too, agree with Your Highness.”
“Then I have nothing more to say.”
“...You honor me beyond measure.”
It had been a tense exchange, with no clear victor or loser.
But if I had to call it, we’d definitely come out ahead.
We’d secured a promise of safety in the Commander’s name and confirmed that Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao’s authority wasn’t so easy to disregard.
The problem was...
Who knows how long that safety will last.
Was this what it felt like to lie on an operating table?
My companions and I were patients.
Instead of kind nurses, the place was crawling with members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and eunuchs armed with blades and spears.
And the surgeon would be none other than the Son of Heaven himself.
This was the imperial palace.
One word from the Emperor, who still hadn’t shown his face, could change our fates.
To have your fate decided by someone you’ve never even seen...
This felt a lot shittier than I’d expected.
Of course, even if the Son of Heaven held the power of life and death, I had no intention of taking it lying down.
The one saving grace was that we hadn’t been given a firm diagnosis yet.
Maybe it would end with a few stitches.
Or maybe terrifying nurses wielding blades and spears instead of anesthetic and surgical instruments would put us to sleep for good.
What happened next would depend on what we did.
No.
I hoped it would.
If the surgeon had already declared us terminal, we’d have to fight for our lives with everything we had.
And Baek Yeon—the head nurse who served closest to the surgeon—had come bearing new information about that.
“By His Majesty the Emperor’s command, Your Highness’s audience has been postponed until tomorrow.”
“Postponed?
Is that what my elder brother said?”
“Yes, Your Highness.”
Zhu Bao wasn’t the only one whose eyes widened at the unexpected news.
Hong Jin’s did, too.
“But before we arrived, I was told...”
“How dare a mere eunuch interrupt, Hong Cheophyeong.
No—Deputy Military Commissioner now, is it?”
They appeared to have met before.
Baek Yeon cut Hong Jin off firmly and continued.
“You will attend to His Highness until you receive word.”
“...Can’t you at least tell us why?”
“I said it was His Majesty’s command.
Do you need another reason?”
Hong Jin had been about to say something, but closed his mouth.
It was the Emperor’s command.
There was no questioning or arguing with that.
I turned the sudden postponement over in my mind.
Why?
Is there a reason?
An audience that had already been arranged had been postponed.
The whims of the powerful were nothing new, but given the situation, I couldn’t help thinking hard about it.
Of course, with everything shrouded in fog, I couldn’t get very far.
“Thousand Captain Jeong.”
“Your orders?”
“Escort His Highness Prince Shangshan inside.
And...”
The moment Baek Yeon’s gray eyes, marked by many years despite his appearance, turned toward me—
Rumble.
I felt his aura tighten around my whole body.
That immense force had been aimed at me alone.
As soon as I realized it, I roused the internal energy sleeping deep in my lower dantian.
Whoosh.
Two invisible forces met across the empty air.
They collided and mingled countless times in the blink of an eye, then finally dispersed like mist.
A voice reached me that no one else could hear.
—Not bad, young man.
Half my strength.
No—not even half of that had gone into that contest of auras.
I’d learned nothing from the exchange.
Instead of answering, I licked my lips.
Baek Yeon gazed at me for a moment, then finished what he’d been saying.
“The others will come as well.”
“Loyalty!”
Jeong Hogun gave a vigorous military salute, then nodded to his subordinates.
A wave of gold surrounded us once more, and we began to move.
Or rather, we were about to.
“Ah, I nearly forgot something.”
Baek Yeon’s quiet voice stopped everyone in their tracks.
He walked up to one of the members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and spoke.
“You dared to draw your sword in front of His Highness.”
Shhk.

Baek Yeon had cut down his subordinate with a hand blade that flashed through the air.
Then he turned to Prince Shangshan and smiled.
“A subordinate’s crime is my own fault.
Please forgive me, Your Highness.”

chapters.title: Chapter 864
paragraphs: “My subordinate’s crime is my own failing. Please forgive me, Your Highness.”
Baek Yeon smiled warmly as he looked at the young prince before him.
Prince Shangshan’s eyes shone with unusual clarity. Reflected in them was Baek Yeon, spattered with his subordinate’s blood.
He looked like a beast facing its prey.
The response came at once.
“Baek Yeon, how dare you—!”
Hong Jin sprang in front of his young lord, his voice boiling with fury. But Baek Yeon paid him no mind.
No—more precisely, he couldn’t afford to.
Someone far more dangerous than any eunuch was staring straight at him.
“This guy. I thought we were going to settle this nicely, but you’ve really crossed the line.”
At the young man’s offhand remark, Baek Yeon’s smile deepened.
“Is there a problem, Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
“There is. A big one. Are you really allowed to do this?”
Jin Taekyung scratched his chin and pointed at the severed head on the ground.
Blood poured without pause from the neck, cut so cleanly it sent a shiver down his spine.
“You commit murder in front of His Highness? Is a Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard allowed to run wild like this?”
“Of course.”
“What?”
“I said I’m allowed. No matter how much power a high official wields—even if he’s a member of the imperial family—I and the Embroidered Uniform Guard serve only one person and obey his will.”
Baek Yeon raised one hand toward the dark sky, then spread both arms toward the vast buildings stretching endlessly behind him.
“The Son of Heaven. Aside from His Majesty the Emperor, who rules this world on Heaven’s behalf, who would dare punish the Embroidered Uniform Guard on a private whim?”
“The only reason I—or rather, the Embroidered Uniform Guard—exist is to serve His Majesty. If anyone tries to undermine his authority or defy him...”
His mouth was still smiling, but his eyes weren’t.

Baek Yeon swept a cold gaze over those around him: the East Depot eunuchs, their faces stiff; Hong Jin and Hyuk Mujin, tense; and finally Jin Taekyung, standing between him and Prince Shangshan. Only then did he continue.
“Whoever they are, they won’t escape death.”
Thud.
Baek Yeon kicked the head. It rolled to a stop at someone’s feet. Jin Taekyung stared down at his leather shoe as blood soaked into it, then spoke.
“So, are you going to claim we’ve committed treason now?”
“Prince Shangshan, committing treason? Ha! That’s a frightening thing to say, my friend.”
Baek Yeon laughed aloud and waved a hand.
“No, no. I merely punished him myself.”
“Punished him?”
“He dared draw his sword in front of His Highness Prince Shangshan. That’s a capital crime. As someone said earlier, shouldn’t he be thoroughly fucked up for it?”
“I appreciate you taking my opinion into account, but it looks like there’s one more person who needs to be fucked up.”
Jin Taekyung laughed along with him.
“The man who drew his sword in front of royalty is dead. What happens to the man who spilled blood?”
“I summarily executed someone who might have become a traitor. I expect I’ll receive due praise and a reward.”
“Who says?”
“You may not know this, but incidents within the Embroidered Uniform Guard are generally resolved quickly. There are only two people who get to decide.”
Jin Taekyung let out a dry laugh.
He could already guess who they were.
One was the Son of Heaven, the very reason the Embroidered Uniform Guard existed. The other...
“The Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard?”
“Correct. You’re sharper than I expected, Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Damn it.”

“There’s another way, so don’t be disheartened just yet. If you want me punished, you can submit a formal petition to His Majesty the Emperor. Every citizen of the Great Nation has that right. Ah, of course...”
Baek Yeon continued as if something had just occurred to him.
“That might be difficult for a martial-world ruffian without even an identity tablet.”
“There is one more way. Want to hear it?”
Jin Taekyung thought for a moment, then shook his head.
“That would be difficult.”
“Why?”
“I want to kill you, but I don’t want to die.”
“The first is absurd nonsense, but the second is a fairly sensible reason. And that answer just saved your life.”
Clank. Clank.
An unpleasant scrape sounded with every step Baek Yeon took.

Clad in golden armor that gleamed even in the dark, he stopped in front of Jin Taekyung. He looked up at the young man, who stood a head taller than he did, then turned his gaze to the young prince visible past Taekyung’s side.
“Your Highness Prince Shangshan. Do you also believe my conduct was disrespectful?”
“Your Highness. I am asking you.”
The prince’s breath trembled. But Baek Yeon’s armor wasn’t the only thing that still shone in the darkness.
“You are... truly arrogant and discourteous.”
Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao trembled, but kept his eyes fixed on Baek Yeon as he continued.
“Even so, I will not blame you. Nor will I ask my elder brother, His Majesty, to punish you.”
Baek Yeon bent at the waist in an exaggerated bow.
“I am most grateful to hear that, but may I ask why?”
“You are my elder brother’s subject, not mine.”
“Both you and I are ultimately His Majesty’s subjects. But if you were my subject, you would not escape death here today. A sovereign must not forgive a disloyal subject.”
At those words, an unreadable emotion passed over Baek Yeon’s face.
It vanished almost at once. Without a word, he turned and gestured to his subordinates with his chin.
“His Highness appears weary from the long journey. Take him inside at once.”
“Loyalty!”
“Oh, and Thousand Captain Jeong, stay behind a moment.”
The Embroidered Uniform Guard soldiers, who’d paused where they stood, closed in around the party once more.
It was impossible to tell whether they were escorting the party or surrounding them. As they moved, Baek Yeon sent a quiet Sound Transmission.
—You’ll regret coming here.
Jin Taekyung’s reply came flying back amid the golden tide flowing toward the Inner City, as though he’d been waiting for it.
—My whole life’s a regret already. Mind your own business and go suck a dick.
Who else would dare say that to the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard?
Baek Yeon let out a dry laugh at the young ruffian’s reply, which defied his expectations yet again. Leaving the East Depot eunuchs behind, he walked away.
Jeong Hogun, who had stayed at Baek Yeon’s order, followed him as a matter of course.
“Is there something you wish to command me?”
“There is. But before hearing an order, an Embroidered Uniform Guard should think for himself.”
“I will watch Prince Shangshan and his party without the slightest lapse.”
“That’s close to the answer I wanted, but not quite.”
“Then...”
“Make it look as though you’re watching them without a lapse, but leave gaps all the same. Make sure someone can slip through and approach them.”
Clank. Clank.
Baek Yeon climbed the stairs that stretched upward without end. Hundreds, even thousands of them. They symbolized the Son of Heaven’s authority.
No matter how high an official’s rank, every time they went to court, they had to climb those stairs drenched in sweat.
Leaving behind their power and their gold and silver treasures.
Reminded of the Son of Heaven’s majesty, which reached all the way to Heaven.
“Watch whom they meet and who comes to see them. Find out everything.”
To catch fish in a net, you first had to spread it wide.
Only then did you draw it tight and haul it in.
Of course, you also had to consider the possibility that something bulky or sharp-toothed might tear through it.
“How is ‘that matter’ I entrusted to you some time ago?”
No answer came. Jeong Hogun lowered his head in silence, and Baek Yeon clicked his tongue softly.
“Cunning bastards.”
“I have nothing to say. I did my best, but...”
“It doesn’t matter. Not yet. But there must not be a second mistake.”
“Of course. Give me the order, and I will carry it out without fail.”
“Without fail? Whatever the order?”
“Yes.”
Baek Yeon suddenly stopped and turned to look at Jeong Hogun. A silent whisper slipped through his slightly parted lips.
—If I ordered you to assassinate His Highness Prince Shangshan, would you do it?
Jeong Hogun’s eyes widened, his pupils wavering. Baek Yeon looked down at his subordinate without a word, then chuckled.
“No need to be so shocked. It was only a joke.”
“A joke...?”
“Yes. But I really am curious about your answer.”
A bead of cold sweat ran down Jeong Hogun’s forehead. He hadn’t even noticed it forming.
His silence did not last long.
“I will follow your orders with my life. If they are the Emperor’s command.”
The smile slowly faded from Baek Yeon’s lips. He studied his subordinate with an odd expression, then smiled faintly again.
“You’re right. That is an answer worthy of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.”
“...I apologize.”
“What are you apologizing for? The Embroidered Uniform Guard lives and dies by the Emperor’s command. Of course we act only according to His Majesty’s will.”
Baek Yeon turned his head.
Far in the distance, he could see a procession of torches and golden armor stretching out one after another.
And though he could not see him now, the prince with dragon’s blood was somewhere within that ironclad escort.
Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.
The young prince might not remember, but the old officer remembered clearly.
The Son of Heaven’s only younger brother. The sole direct member of the imperial family to survive the most brutal power struggle in history.
The child he had last seen more than a decade ago had grown considerably. In body and in mind.
“...Which makes him all the more dangerous.”
Jeong Hogun lifted his head at Baek Yeon’s whispered words.
Baek Yeon waved a hand as if nothing had happened, then spoke again. Not a trace of a smile remained on his stern face.
“Remember one thing.”
“Give me your command.”
“Once they’ve set foot in this imperial palace, no one is to be allowed to leave.”
Jeong Hogun understood at once.
Baek Yeon wasn’t speaking only of Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard had to watch more than the prince with dragon’s blood. There was also the martial-world ruffian who dared bear the title of Divine Dragon.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
The dragon was a mythical spiritual creature that symbolized the Son of Heaven alone.
Yet the young prince had brought an uninvited Divine Dragon into the imperial palace where the Son of Heaven resided.
He had made that ruffian, who disregarded the laws of the Great Nation, his guard. He had defended him and taken him under his protection.
No one could be certain what that choice would bring.
Not Jeong Hogun. Not even Baek Yeon, who had anticipated the situation and let it happen.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung they knew had always been like that.
He always overturned everyone’s expectations, bringing storms and flames that swept in from every direction.
Fwoosh.
In the darkness, a fierce wind blew from somewhere, setting the torches flickering.

“There is.
But before hearing an order, an Embroidered Uniform Guard should think for himself.”
“I will watch Prince Shangshan and his party without the slightest lapse.”
“That’s close to the answer I wanted, but not quite.”
“Then...”
“Make it look as though you’re watching them without a lapse, but leave gaps all the same.
Make sure someone can slip through and approach them.”
Clank.
Clank.
Baek Yeon climbed the stairs that stretched upward without end.
Hundreds, even thousands of them.
They symbolized the Son of Heaven’s authority.
No matter how high an official’s rank, every time they went to court, they had to climb those stairs drenched in sweat.
Leaving behind their power and their gold and silver treasures.
Reminded of the Son of Heaven’s majesty, which reached all the way to Heaven.
“Watch whom they meet and who comes to see them.
Find out everything.”
To catch fish in a net, you first had to spread it wide.
Only then did you draw it tight and haul it in.
Of course, you also had to consider the possibility that something bulky or sharp-toothed might tear through it.
“How is ‘that matter’ I entrusted to you some time ago?”
No answer came.
Jeong Hogun lowered his head in silence, and Baek Yeon clicked his tongue softly.
“Cunning bastards.”
“I have nothing to say.
I did my best, but...”
“It doesn’t matter.
Not yet.
But there must not be a second mistake.”
“Of course.
Give me the order, and I will carry it out without fail.”
“Without fail?
Whatever the order?”
“Yes.”
Baek Yeon suddenly stopped and turned to look at Jeong Hogun.
A silent whisper slipped through his slightly parted lips.
—If I ordered you to assassinate His Highness Prince Shangshan, would you do it?
Jeong Hogun’s eyes widened, his pupils wavering.
Baek Yeon looked down at his subordinate without a word, then chuckled.
“No need to be so shocked.
It was only a joke.”
“A joke...?”
“Yes.
But I really am curious about your answer.”
A bead of cold sweat ran down Jeong Hogun’s forehead.
He hadn’t even noticed it forming.
His silence did not last long.
“I will follow your orders with my life.
If they are the Emperor’s command.”
The smile slowly faded from Baek Yeon’s lips.
He studied his subordinate with an odd expression, then smiled faintly again.
“You’re right.
That is an answer worthy of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.”
“...I apologize.”
“What are you apologizing for?
The Embroidered Uniform Guard lives and dies by the Emperor’s command.
Of course we act only according to His Majesty’s will.”
Baek Yeon turned his head.
Far in the distance, he could see a procession of torches and golden armor stretching out one after another.
And though he could not see him now, the prince with dragon’s blood was somewhere within that ironclad escort.
Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.
The young prince might not remember, but the old officer remembered clearly.
The Son of Heaven’s only younger brother.
The sole direct member of the imperial family to survive the most brutal power struggle in history.
The child he had last seen more than a decade ago had grown considerably.
In body and in mind.
“...Which makes him all the more dangerous.”
Jeong Hogun lifted his head at Baek Yeon’s whispered words.
Baek Yeon waved a hand as if nothing had happened, then spoke again.
Not a trace of a smile remained on his stern face.
“Remember one thing.”
“Give me your command.”
“Once they’ve set foot in this imperial palace, no one is to be allowed to leave.”
Jeong Hogun understood at once.
Baek Yeon wasn’t speaking only of Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard had to watch more than the prince with dragon’s blood.
There was also the martial-world ruffian who dared bear the title of Divine Dragon.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
The dragon was a mythical spiritual creature that symbolized the Son of Heaven alone.
Yet the young prince had brought an uninvited Divine Dragon into the imperial palace where the Son of Heaven resided.
He had made that ruffian, who disregarded the laws of the Great Nation, his guard.
He had defended him and taken him under his protection.
No one could be certain what that choice would bring.
Not Jeong Hogun.
Not even Baek Yeon, who had anticipated the situation and let it happen.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung they knew had always been like that.
He always overturned everyone’s expectations, bringing storms and flames that swept in from every direction.
Fwoosh.
In the darkness, a fierce wind blew from somewhere, setting the torches flickering.

chapters.title: Chapter 865
paragraphs: A person’s body and mind are like a bowstring.
Drawn taut, then released all at once.
Once the tension lets up, exhaustion catches up with you.
That was true even for me, after weathering countless crises. For a child barely twelve or thirteen, it went without saying.
Click.
Careful not to wake his young lord, Hong Jin closed the door with the utmost care and whispered to me,
“He must have been exhausted. He fell asleep in no time.”
Soft, even breathing came through the crack in the closed door.
Once I was sure Prince Shangshan was fast asleep, I glanced out the window.
Down below, amid the swaying torchlight, members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard stood like iron towers in their golden armor.
You bastards. It’s dark enough already. Why don’t you clock out on time for once?
Of course, that wasn’t going to happen.
From what I’d seen, those guys would risk not just overtime but their lives to carry out an order.
Murim martial artists were all crazy in their own way, but the Embroidered Uniform Guard were hunting dogs, blindly loyal to the Son of Heaven.
“Watching us like that won’t change anything. They won’t leave their posts for even a moment.”
Hong Jin surveyed the torches and guards surrounding the pavilion as if they were laying siege to it, then added, “That’s how the Changwei operate.”
“Changwei?”
“Oh, it’s a collective name for the East Depot and the Embroidered Uniform Guard. As I told you, Young Master Jin, I was once part of one of them.”
I knew Hong Jin had belonged to the East Depot, but there was still plenty I wanted to ask him.
As if he’d read my mind, Hong Jin spoke first.
“Now that it’s finally just the two of us, shall we talk for a bit?”
I’d be grateful if he did.
I nodded, and Hong Jin and I walked downstairs together.
We’d already sent away the Embroidered Uniform Guard, along with the palace attendants who were more or less there to keep an eye on us for them.
Even though I could see everything happening inside the pavilion as clearly as if it were in the palm of my hand, Hong Jin was still deeply uneasy about leaving Prince Shangshan alone.
“Young Master Jin, do you think it’s all right?”
“There’s no need to worry. I’m nearby, and more importantly, I left that rascal Mujin with His Highness as a precaution.”
“Right. That makes me even more worried.”
Thank goodness Hyuk Mujin hadn’t heard that. I stepped into an empty room.
As befitted a pavilion belonging to the imperial palace, it was spacious, with a faint fragrance drifting among the antique furnishings.
Best of all, there’s no chance anyone’s bugging us.
Back in the modern world, I’d worried about being overheard whenever I had an important conversation. Murim was old-fashioned enough that I could talk without a care.
“Finally, I can breathe a little. Don’t you think?”
Hong Jin seemed to feel much the same way. He brought a lit candelabra over to the window to brighten the dark room, then sat down and spoke, looking tired.
“I’m sure you have a lot you want to ask me, Young Master Jin, but could I speak first?”
“Go ahead.”
“Don’t provoke him more than necessary. Whatever you do.”
He hadn’t said who he meant, but I knew at once.
“Baek Yeon?”
“That’s right. Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. Keep as much distance between you and him as you can.”
I didn’t ask why. There was no need.
He commanded the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was an exceptionally skilled Supreme Peak master, and was the military officer the Son of Heaven trusted most.
Any one of those would have been reason enough for caution. All three together left nothing to discuss.
But...
“I think we’ve already gotten a little too close for that.”
Hong Jin sighed.
“I know. I saw everything with my own two eyes. I’m just asking you to be careful from now on.”
His worry showed in his expression, his voice, even the way he spoke.
The Hong Jin I knew had plenty of nerve. The East Depot, made up of eunuchs, was a ruthless organization that served as the Emperor’s human-cleanup crew alongside the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

He seemed to have held a fairly high position there, so he must have been through all sorts of hell. He’d even sneered while dealing with Jeong Hogun and the other guards, and with the East Depot eunuchs.
Until Baek Yeon appeared.
“Is there another reason I don’t know about?”
Hong Jin’s answer made his concern clear.
“Thirty thousand. That’s how many people Baek Yeon captured and killed in the last coup.”

“How did the fourth prince, already sidelined in the struggle for succession, manage to seize the throne of the Great Nation? Because he was exceptionally capable? No. That wasn’t enough. He needed a cause, and he needed people. No one becomes the Son of Heaven by their own strength alone.”
Hong Jin rushed through the words, then took a long-stemmed tobacco pipe from inside his clothes and put it to his mouth.
Before long, pungent smoke rose around him. His face looked especially dark through the haze as he continued.

“Baek Yeon was already head of the Embroidered Uniform Guard long before I entered the imperial palace. He had the late Emperor’s full trust from a young age, and for a time, he even taught the Crown Prince martial arts.”
“The Crown Prince—you mean the one...?”
“That’s right. So when Baek Yeon helped the fourth prince stage a coup, everyone was stunned. No one thought he, of all people, would betray the late Emperor and the Crown Prince.”
Hoooo.
Smoke curled up from Hong Jin’s lips. Through the pale haze, it was almost as if the past he remembered were passing before him.

“It began in an instant and was over just as quickly. They moved so secretly that even the East Depot couldn’t do a thing. No—perhaps it’s more accurate to say we were caught off guard because we never saw it coming.”
The coup began in the dead of night and was over around dawn.
The pounding of hooves echoed across the Imperial Capital until daybreak, and the screams never stopped.

“The coup was... perfect enough to make your skin crawl. Every civil and military official had gathered to celebrate His Majesty the Emperor’s birthday, along with members of the imperial family from every corner of the land. Security was tighter than ever against any possible threat. Except for one thing.”
This wasn’t some village headman’s birthday. It was the birthday of the Emperor, ruler of an entire continent.
I could almost see it all before me: the packed crowds that day, and the dazzling golden armor of the guards who had sealed off the imperial palace.
“...The Embroidered Uniform Guard. They were in charge of the palace defenses.”
Hong Jin gave a bitter smile and nodded.
“Yes. That’s right.”
Everything had been prepared down to the last detail.

Baek Yeon and the guards who followed him took control of the imperial palace in an instant. As everyone looked on in shock, the fourth prince alone rose to his feet and stepped onto the stage prepared for him, his expression calm.
It was the moment the history of the Great Nation changed.
“And then... the purge began.”
The unexpected spectacle was over, but no one left their seats. No—no one could leave.
The people who had arrived as nothing more than spectators were forced to become actors in the next performance.

“Those who submitted at once survived. Those who resisted were dragged off to the prisons controlled by the Embroidered Uniform Guard. The imperial family had it a little better, at least. At first, they were only confined.”
The Emperor—no, the late Emperor—was already old. He was locked inside his residence. The Crown Prince and his wife, and the rest of the imperial family, were no exception.
They endured day after day under relentless watch, trembling at the screams that rang out day and night beyond the high walls surrounding them.
Waiting for their turn to come.
“Countless people died in the process. More families than anyone could count were wiped out. And...”
Hong Jin let his voice trail off before adding, “The man who led the purge was the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. No—the Blood Envoy, Baek Yeon.”
“The Blood Envoy...”
“Every time I hear it, I think how well that sobriquet suits him. Don’t you?”
Hong Jin’s lips curled into a smile, but it was feeble and vanished almost immediately.

“Young Master Jin. Back then, I couldn’t do anything. I failed to detect the treason, so I was incompetent as a subject. And all I could do was watch it happen, so I was powerless. But one thing hasn’t changed, then or now.”
Tap.
Hong Jin knocked the ash from his pipe. He looked up as if he could see through the ceiling to where the young prince lay sleeping, then continued.
“I must protect His Highness Prince Shangshan. That was the late Emperor’s final wish. It’s also the last act of loyalty I can offer as a servant who was both incompetent and powerless.”
His voice fell silent.
In the heavy silence, I turned over what he’d told me, then spoke abruptly.
“I’m not sure that’s really loyalty.”
“Hmm?”
“A subject wanting to protect his lord and a parent worrying about a child are two different things. And from what I’ve seen of you, Deputy Military Commissioner, it’s more like the latter.”
“What are you trying to say?”
“It’s simple. His Highness Prince Shangshan isn’t just a child who needs someone to protect him.”
Hong Jin sighed.
“Young Master Jin, I’m sorry, but he’s still young. He’s only thirteen.”

“That’s right. Only thirteen—and already able to make the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, a man whose influence could knock birds from the sky, bow his head. Already able to keep his composure while people die right in front of him.”
Sometimes. Maybe even fairly often.
People caught up in their personal feelings make the wrong call.
Even if that person is a eunuch from the East Depot who’s been through hell and back.
I held Hong Jin’s frozen gaze and continued.
“His Highness Prince Shangshan isn’t a child who needs someone else to protect him. He’s been a king for a long time already. He just hasn’t fully come into his own yet.”
“Young Master Jin, you...”

“If all he wanted was to survive, he could throw himself at the Emperor’s feet tomorrow and beg for his life. He could plead that he had no idea what crime he’d committed and ask to be spared just this once. Assuming, of course, that his desperate plea stirs the Emperor’s tender heart.”
“But you have something else in mind, don’t you, Deputy Military Commissioner?”
Hong Jin stared at me, his face set, then asked in a dry voice, “What makes you think that?”

“At a time when you should be bending over backward to please the Emperor, you dared to bring martial-world ruffians into the imperial palace. You dared to speak provocatively in front of the East Depot and the Embroidered Uniform Guard. And...”
I suddenly turned around and continued slowly.
“Late tonight, you brought an uninvited guest all the way here without the Embroidered Uniform Guard noticing.”
At that moment—
Fwoosh. Whoosh.
The three candles Hong Jin had lit when he entered the room went out at once.
I looked from Hong Jin to the black figure that had appeared out of thin air, then back again.
“So, when are you going to introduce us?”

chapters.title: Chapter 866
paragraphs: An uninvited guest turning up at night was never welcome.
Especially when he was a Supreme Peak master with extraordinary concealment techniques.
“Young Master Jin, I know it’s late, but let me introduce you. This is...”
“No need. I barged in without permission, so the least I can do is introduce myself.”
Slide.
The stranger interrupted Hong Jin and pulled down his mask, revealing a smooth, clean-shaven face.
His build was so androgynous it was hard to guess his gender, and he looked a good ten years younger than Hong Jin.
Then there was his martial prowess. He had reached Supreme Peak.
Put all those clues together, and it wasn’t hard to guess who the uninvited guest was.
“The East Depot?”
The stranger nodded.
“You’ve got a sharp eye.”
As if turning up uninvited weren’t enough, he was talking down to me, too.
I didn’t like it, but in a way, that made things easier.
I could do the same.
“Well, if I couldn’t figure out that much, I might as well go die.”
“And you don’t hold back when you speak.”
“Think my mouth’s the only thing I don’t hold back?”
“Good. Very good.”
The stranger smiled soundlessly and clasped his hands in a formal salute.
“Let me introduce myself properly. I’m Ma Sanbao, Brush-Holding Eunuch of the East Depot.”
Brush-Holding Eunuch of the East Depot? Ma Sanbao?
The title sounded important enough, but his name was on the level of Gaettong from next door.
Hong Jin saw the question in my eyes and spoke up.
“The Brush-Holding Eunuch is the East Depot’s second-in-command. In terms of rank, he comes right after the Chief Eunuch.”
I stared at the stranger—or rather, Ma Sanbao.
His position was more impressive than I’d imagined, but I was even more curious why a big shot like the East Depot’s second-in-command had come here in secret at this late hour.
Especially after I’d seen how that old eunuch treated Hong Jin earlier.
“Hadn’t you already fallen out with the East Depot? Judging by what happened earlier, things didn’t look good between you.”
Ma Sanbao laughed again, though I’d asked Hong Jin.
“You’re certainly no ordinary young man. To bring that up so casually right in front of me...”
“I wasn’t asking you.”
“Doesn’t matter. I’m glad it looked that way. If even someone on our side was fooled, the Embroidered Uniform Guard won’t suspect a thing.”
Fooled?
I stopped short and looked at Hong Jin.
“...That was an act? All of it?”
“To be precise, it was planned from the start. But I wouldn’t call it an act. He’s disliked me for a long time.”
Ma Sanbao nodded at Hong Jin’s answer.
“Mm. A long time. More than thirty years, if I remember right.”
“You chose your man well, Ma Constable. Or should I call you Eunuch Ma now?”
“My, you’ve grown even more mischievous since I last saw you. A man like me would never have dared dream of taking your place. I’ve only been keeping it for you.”
“Not at all.”
Hong Jin’s answer was firm.
“You’re more than qualified for that position. You were then, and you are now.”
“...Good grief. Come to think of it, I forgot to greet you.”
Shaking his head, Ma Sanbao patted Hong Jin’s shoulder. His face held equal parts bitterness and joy.
“Even if the timing couldn’t be worse, I’m glad to see you again, even like this.”
“Likewise.”
Watching two men without balls have an emotional reunion, I felt hot tears begin to run down my face—
No, I didn’t.
An emotional reunion, my ass.
They hadn’t even told me what was going on. Why the hell would I cry?
Still, even I had to admit there was something heartwarming about the sight of them gripping each other’s shoulders.
And beyond the sentiment, Ma Sanbao was the East Depot’s second-in-command.
Nothing in their conversation so far had sounded like bad news.
A secret pact.
They must have arranged this beforehand. I just didn’t know where it had begun or how far it went.
I didn’t have to wait long for an explanation. The two finished their brief reunion and took turns speaking.
“Eunuch Ma and I are from the same cohort. We first set foot in the imperial palace on the same day.”
“And got cut on the same day, too. Remember? You were right ahead of me in line.”
“Was I?”
“I remember it clearly. You didn’t let out a single scream. I thought you were one tough bastard.”
I listened for a moment, then asked, feeling queasy. My tone was a little more polite than before.
“Um, when you say you both got cut on the same day...”
“What else would it be? That.”
“That’s right. That.”
I’d suspected as much, but was this for real?
Ball buddies.
So this was the amazing imperial palace.
Childhood buddies? Coworkers who’d started on the same day? Neither could hold a candle to these two.
They’d been cut together before entering the palace. Their bond had to be on a whole other level.
“We joined the East Depot around the same time and rose through the ranks together.”
“That sounds about right. Except you were always one step ahead of me.”
“At times, perhaps. But Cang Gong always trusted you most, Eunuch Ma. And when it came to martial arts talent, no one in the East Depot could match you. Certainly not me.”
I didn’t know how much of their conversation was true, but it suddenly struck me that Hong Jin’s assessment of Ma Sanbao’s martial arts was probably not exaggerated in the slightest.
The qi I’d sensed from Ma Sanbao the moment I saw him was in no way inferior to mine or Baek Yeon’s.
Of course, internal energy isn’t everything.
I muttered to myself and looked Ma Sanbao over from head to toe.
His height. The length of his arms and legs. Which muscles were especially developed, and what weapon he might use.
At this point, it was practically an occupational hazard bordering on a mental disorder. But sizing up someone I’d just met was an important habit.
Provided I didn’t needlessly offend him.
“Young man, you’ve got a remarkably keen eye.”
At Ma Sanbao’s sudden remark, I clicked my tongue inwardly.
“I was about to say the same about you.”
“What, surprised I noticed so quickly?”
“Mm. A little.”
“An old habit. I may not be a Murim martial artist like you, but I have to stay alert wherever I go.”
I’d examined him as discreetly as possible, in a fraction of a second—too quickly for him to have noticed.
Yet Ma Sanbao had caught me while talking with Hong Jin. His Qi Sense was better than that of most Supreme Peak masters.
So this is the East Depot.
The East Depot and the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
I’d already heard what these two organizations, collectively known as the Changwei, did.
Assassination of important figures. Surveillance, intelligence gathering, and more.
They were intelligence agents trained to the limit, skilled assassins, and soldiers.
And with the Son of Heaven’s dazzling authority behind them, I’d heard they also served as a law enforcement agency.
Their influence and military strength had to be immense.
Even the low-ranking Embroidered Uniform Guard and East Depot eunuchs I’ve seen were no ordinary people.
“No ordinary people” didn’t begin to cover it.
Even the weakest were Supreme First Rate, and more than half were Peak masters.
On the way to the imperial palace, I’d seen hundreds of Peak masters with my own eyes.
If those were only a fraction of their forces, what they had yet to reveal was terrifying.
And if the imperial palace joined hands with Dark Heaven—if, by some chance, it really came to that...
A cold shiver ran up my spine. My face, reflected in Ma Sanbao’s eyes, had stiffened without me noticing.
“You’re wary of me.”
“Let’s call it questions rather than wariness. For now.”
“For now?”
“I don’t need you to tell me you two are close. What I want to know is that there still seem to be a lot of facts I haven’t heard.”
“Yes, I suppose there is.”
Ma Sanbao dropped into an empty chair and continued.
“How much do I need to tell you to answer your questions?”
“Everything. From beginning to end.”
“Everything would take too long to tell tonight. But there’s one thing I should tell you first.”
“Let’s hear it, then.”

“About a month ago, I sent someone a secret letter. It said that some members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard were heading north under concealed identities. I also included my own suspicion that they were bound for Shanxi Province.”
Hong Jin picked up the story quietly.
“Thanks to the information Eunuch Ma sent me, I had time to prepare, even if it wasn’t much. Asking Young Master Jin for help was a decision I made after careful thought.”
This was news to me.
I’d assumed Hong Jin had chosen me because he was desperate and had no one else to turn to.
But I was wrong.
Hong Jin had thought it through carefully and asked me for help.
And through it all, someone had been helping him from behind the scenes.
No matter how capable Hong Jin was, he couldn’t keep track of everything happening in the imperial capital from over ten thousand li away.
But the East Depot’s second-in-command could.
The East Depot had spies planted throughout the land, watching for any movement. There was no question they’d know what was happening in the imperial capital—their own front yard.
That still didn’t answer everything.
“I understand that you helped save His Highness Prince Shangshan. But...”
“I think I know what you’re going to say. Yes, you’re right. I’ve sworn loyalty to His Majesty.”
Ma Sanbao spoke before I could continue. Then, in a low voice, he added:
“Not the traitor sitting on the throne now. The late Emperor.”
“Do you know why I’ve remained in the imperial palace all this time? How I’ve managed it?”
Tap. Tap.
Drops of blood fell through the gaps in his white-knuckled fist. The East Depot’s second-in-command went on in a sharp voice unlike any I’d heard from him before.
“Because there was something I had to do. Because I had to endure whatever hardships came and wait for my moment...!”
He couldn’t shout the words aloud. The cry struck the internal energy I’d spread around us and faded away.
Ma Sanbao’s lips trembled as he let emotions hidden for more than a decade show on his face.
He looked at his longtime friend and spoke in a voice seething with feeling.
“Hong Jin. Hong Constable. My friend and comrade. The time has finally come. We can’t put it off any longer.”
“Eunuch Ma. You don’t mean...”
“I do.”
Rumble.
A thunderous boom rang out without warning, and the dark sky blazed with light. Rain poured and lightning flashed beyond the window behind Ma Sanbao as he ground out the words.
“Let’s set right, with our own hands, the sky that traitor has thrown into chaos.”

I could do the same.

“Good.

chapters.title: Chapter 867
paragraphs: Rumble.
Thunder rolled across the sky. As dazzling lightning flashed and torrential rain came pouring down, the palace attendants hurried about.

Eunuchs and palace maids scurried toward the quarters of the consorts they served, worried that rainwater might be leaking in. The Embroidered Uniform Guards stationed throughout the imperial palace stood their ground beneath their broad-brimmed hats.
Everyone who worked in the imperial palace had a role to play.
Do your job well, and you were rewarded. Fail to, and you were punished.
Yet one man strolled through the relentless downpour at his leisure. He was one of the few people in this vast palace who needn’t concern himself with rewards or punishments.
No—in fact, it was closer to the opposite.
He wielded such immense authority that he could reward or punish others without the Son of Heaven’s approval.
And yet no palace attendant dared try to catch his eye or get close to him.
Not even the rain pouring ceaselessly down at that very moment.
Whoosh.
Though he walked through the downpour, not a drop of water touched him.
His half-white hair, tousled as it pleased, was bone-dry. His golden armor, polished with oil-treated cloth, still gleamed brilliantly.
It was a strange, almost unreal sight, but then, he was no ordinary man.
Immense authority wasn’t all he possessed.
Raw power.
Martial prowess far beyond the limits of human ability.
He had the power to make the unreal real. With an important meeting ahead of him, he simply didn’t want to get wet.
Vwoom.
The air trembled with his profound internal energy. Rain struck an invisible barrier and scattered in every direction, unable to touch him.
“It’s been quiet lately, but now it’s really coming down...”
Muttering as he looked up at the sky flashing with lightning, the man resumed his steps. No one dared stand in his way.
No one had in the past. No one did now. And no one would in the future.
Clank. Rumble.
The mere sight of him approaching from afar was enough.
The Embroidered Uniform Guards peered out from beneath their deeply lowered hats. Without a moment’s hesitation, they opened the firmly shut gates and kept their heads bowed until he had passed.
The same was true of those quietly performing their duties out of sight.
“Open the way.”
At his sudden command, the vast garden, filled with all manner of rare flowers and plants, shimmered like a heat haze.
Whoosh.
Even the foreign trees and flowers that had stood tall against the fierce wind and rain lowered their heads.
Thick leaves and branches slid aside, revealing a hidden path where only those granted permission could set foot.
Beautiful flowers have thorns.

The imperial palace’s gardens were no different. An unwelcome guest fooled by their beauty into stepping inside would find himself surrounded by countless mechanisms and formations and riddled with holes.
And it wasn’t just the gardens.
The imperial palace itself was a den of dangers, a demon-slaying battleground—a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords in the truest sense.
Anyone without permission would die.
Even someone whose martial prowess reached the heavens could not be sure of surviving.
As the man passed through five gates and dozens of pavilions, he was reminded of that once more. At last, he reached his destination and stopped.
Qianqing Palace.
Beneath a signboard inscribed in a bold, soaring hand, two middle-aged men stood like iron towers. They lowered their heads in greeting.
“You’ve arrived.”
“You’ve arrived.”
Their voices and expressions were as alike as if they were one person.
Their faces, too, made it plain they had been born of the same womb on the same day.
The twins continued politely.
“Please wait a moment.”
“Please wait a moment.”
The man frowned. Not because they were speaking in unison again, despite how many times he had told them not to, but because of the strong smell of blood coming from them.
“Looks like you had a guest.”
“Yes.”
“Yes.”
“Did you kill him? Who was behind it?”
“He took his own life just before we could capture him.”
“He took his own life just before—”
“Enough. How many times have I told you once is enough? So you failed to take the intruder alive?”
The twins blinked at him, looking unsure what to do, then mumbled under their breath.
“He had a potent poison hidden beneath one of his molars.”
“He had a potent poison hidden—no, we did everything we could, but we couldn’t stop him. We beg your forgiveness.”
The man clicked his tongue softly.
The fact that the intruder had made it this far was proof of his extraordinary martial prowess.
Failing to capture him and learn who was behind him was a painful mistake, but something mattered more than reprimanding the twins right now.
“Don’t tell me he got inside the palace.”
“Of course not.”
“Of course not.”
At least that’s a relief. The man asked another question.
“Is he inside?”
“He’s waiting.”
“He’s waiting.”
The man nodded, glanced up at the signboard, then stepped forward.
Qianqing Palace. Qianqing—“clear sky.” Those two characters seemed a poor fit for today.
Step. Step.
The palace interior was quiet.
Not a person—or even a rat—could be seen. Only the countless paintings and works of art hanging on the walls glimmered in the faint light.
But what he could see wasn’t everything.
With every step, the man felt eyes following him. Shadows ready to rush out and cut him to pieces if he posed even the slightest threat, whoever he might be.
At last, he stopped. Before him was a vast space prepared for one person alone, and there its master waited.
No—the master of all under heaven.
“I, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, have come at the summons of Your Majesty, the august Emperor.”
At that moment—
Rustle.
The colorful silk curtains draped around the room stirred.
Through the thin silk, amid wisps of faintly fragrant smoke, he glimpsed the back of someone dressed in dazzling white.
“You’ve come.”
A quiet voice echoed through the room. At first, it sounded calm, almost languid.
The Son of Heaven of the Great Nation continued slowly, as if speaking to himself.
“I had a bad dream. A dream that someone was trying to harm me.”
“I fought for a long time, covered in blood. They came at me from somewhere, without end, and I cut them down without end. Only when I finally woke did I realize it hadn’t been a mere dream.”
Baek Yeon raised his head in silence. Pale smoke drifted from between the Son of Heaven’s lips.
“So you’ve turned to poppy again.”
“Does this look like poppy to you?”
“Forgive me, but that is exactly what it looks like to me.”
“You’re wrong. This isn’t poppy. It’s medicine—the only thing that can heal me.”
Baek Yeon’s brow twitched.
“Your Majesty, may I speak with you about something important?”
The Son of Heaven didn’t answer. Instead, he flicked his long, wide sleeve.
Swish.
With a faint rustle, the presences surrounding them withdrew like the tide. Baek Yeon straightened from his bow, his voice cold.
“Your Majesty, with the great undertaking nearly complete, why would you disgrace yourself like this?”
If anyone else had been there, they would have covered their eyes and ears.
Baek Yeon’s tone was far too sharp for a subject speaking to his ruler. It was more than insolent—it was defiant.
Yet the Son of Heaven didn’t answer this time, either. The ruler of the world gave a low laugh instead. Only after a long while did he speak.
“The great undertaking. Yes. There was a great undertaking.”
“Please don’t forget the promise we made that day.”
“Forget?”
The Son of Heaven muttered with a short, incredulous laugh.
“I haven’t forgotten. Not for a single moment since that day.”
His voice was as weak as a sick man’s.
But Baek Yeon’s eyes, fixed on the Son of Heaven, didn’t waver. They were sunk deep and steady.
“They’ve already begun to move. Before everything falls apart, remember that you must put things back where they belong.”
After a brief silence, the Son of Heaven nodded quietly.
He had come too far to turn back. Once no more than the fourth prince, he now ruled all under heaven. And he had become a man who could no longer get by without poppy.
Wasn’t it said that a horse racing across the wilderness never looked back?
Even the Son of Heaven, who stood above all people, was no exception.
He was a horse that could no longer stop of its own will. Even if it collapsed coughing up blood, it had to keep running toward its destination.
Crack.
His hand clenched instinctively, snapping the ornate long-stemmed tobacco pipe. The Son of Heaven stared at the broken pieces in his palm, then closed his fist tightly around them.
Thump.
The rough pieces dug into his palm. Pain flared like a burn, and little by little, his mind began to clear.
“Ah.”
As if worshiping the heavens, the Son of Heaven tilted his head back toward the ceiling and groaned with his eyes closed.
Baek Yeon watched impassively.
“Shall I call for the imperial physician?”
“No need. Not for an imperial physician.”
The Son of Heaven opened his eyes and continued, his voice clearer now.
“Tomorrow, I’ll meet that child in the audience hall.”
“That child would be...”
“Zhu Bao. I wonder how much my... only younger brother has grown.”
Baek Yeon nodded.
“You can look forward to it. He’s grown even more than Your Majesty expects.”
“Which means he’s become even more dangerous.”
Baek Yeon pressed his lips together, but the Son of Heaven understood.
All sorts of bugs gather around a tempting meal.
Now that Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had appeared in the Imperial Capital, the enemies who resented him would surely draw the blades they had kept hidden beneath their sleeves.
Just like the nameless assassin who had come here before Baek Yeon today.
“Baek Yeon, this must never happen again. Remember that.”
His voice was different now, cold as ice. Baek Yeon faltered, then answered with a faint smile.
“I will engrave Your Majesty’s words into my bones. Please forgive my disloyalty until now.”
Flutter.
In response, the Son of Heaven merely waved his sleeve. Baek Yeon turned and began walking away.
After only a few steps, he stopped.
“And what of that man?”
“If you mean...”
“Zhu Bao. The Murim martial artist who came with him.”
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
Baek Yeon thought carefully about the man who had suddenly come to mind. A long while passed before he spoke.
“I don’t know.”
He had interrogated and killed tens of thousands on the battlefield, and tens of thousands more in the imperial palace.
But that was the best answer Baek Yeon could give.

Muttering as he looked up at the sky flashing with lightning, the man resumed his steps.
No one dared stand in his way.
No one had in the past.
No one did now.
And no one would in the future.
Clank.
Rumble.
The mere sight of him approaching from afar was enough.
The Embroidered Uniform Guards peered out from beneath their deeply lowered hats.
Without a moment’s hesitation, they opened the firmly shut gates and kept their heads bowed until he had passed.
The same was true of those quietly performing their duties out of sight.
“Open the way.”
At his sudden command, the vast garden, filled with all manner of rare flowers and plants, shimmered like a heat haze.
Whoosh.
Even the foreign trees and flowers that had stood tall against the fierce wind and rain lowered their heads.
Thick leaves and branches slid aside, revealing a hidden path where only those granted permission could set foot.
Beautiful flowers have thorns.
The imperial palace’s gardens were no different.
An unwelcome guest fooled by their beauty into stepping inside would find himself surrounded by countless mechanisms and formations and riddled with holes.
And it wasn’t just the gardens.
The imperial palace itself was a den of dangers, a demon-slaying battleground—a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords in the truest sense.
Anyone without permission would die.
Even someone whose martial prowess reached the heavens could not be sure of surviving.
As the man passed through five gates and dozens of pavilions, he was reminded of that once more.
At last, he reached his destination and stopped.
Qianqing Palace.
Beneath a signboard inscribed in a bold, soaring hand, two middle-aged men stood like iron towers.
They lowered their heads in greeting.
“You’ve arrived.”
“You’ve arrived.”
Their voices and expressions were as alike as if they were one person.
Their faces, too, made it plain they had been born of the same womb on the same day.
The twins continued politely.
“Please wait a moment.”
“Please wait a moment.”
The man frowned.
Not because they were speaking in unison again, despite how many times he had told them not to, but because of the strong smell of blood coming from them.
“Looks like you had a guest.”
“Yes.”
“Yes.”
“Did you kill him?
Who was behind it?”
“He took his own life just before we could capture him.”
“He took his own life just before—”
“Enough.
How many times have I told you once is enough?
So you failed to take the intruder alive?”
The twins blinked at him, looking unsure what to do, then mumbled under their breath.
“He had a potent poison hidden beneath one of his molars.”
“He had a potent poison hidden—no, we did everything we could, but we couldn’t stop him.
We beg your forgiveness.”
The man clicked his tongue softly.
The fact that the intruder had made it this far was proof of his extraordinary martial prowess.
Failing to capture him and learn who was behind him was a painful mistake, but something mattered more than reprimanding the twins right now.
“Don’t tell me he got inside the palace.”
“Of course not.”
“Of course not.”
At least that’s a relief.
The man asked another question.
“Is he inside?”
“He’s waiting.”
“He’s waiting.”
The man nodded, glanced up at the signboard, then stepped forward.
Qianqing Palace.
Qianqing—“clear sky.” Those two characters seemed a poor fit for today.
Step.
Step.
The palace interior was quiet.
Not a person—or even a rat—could be seen.
Only the countless paintings and works of art hanging on the walls glimmered in the faint light.
But what he could see wasn’t everything.
With every step, the man felt eyes following him.
Shadows ready to rush out and cut him to pieces if he posed even the slightest threat, whoever he might be.
At last, he stopped.
Before him was a vast space prepared for one person alone, and there its master waited.
No—the master of all under heaven.
“I, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, have come at the summons of Your Majesty, the august Emperor.”
At that moment—
Rustle.
The colorful silk curtains draped around the room stirred.
Through the thin silk, amid wisps of faintly fragrant smoke, he glimpsed the back of someone dressed in dazzling white.
“You’ve come.”
A quiet voice echoed through the room.
At first, it sounded calm, almost languid.
The Son of Heaven of the Great Nation continued slowly, as if speaking to himself.
“I had a bad dream.
A dream that someone was trying to harm me.”
“I fought for a long time, covered in blood.
They came at me from somewhere, without end, and I cut them down without end.
Only when I finally woke did I realize it hadn’t been a mere dream.”
Baek Yeon raised his head in silence.
Pale smoke drifted from between the Son of Heaven’s lips.
“So you’ve turned to poppy again.”
“Does this look like poppy to you?”
“Forgive me, but that is exactly what it looks like to me.”
“You’re wrong.
This isn’t poppy.
It’s medicine—the only thing that can heal me.”
Baek Yeon’s brow twitched.
“Your Majesty, may I speak with you about something important?”
The Son of Heaven didn’t answer.
Instead, he flicked his long, wide sleeve.
Swish.
With a faint rustle, the presences surrounding them withdrew like the tide.
Baek Yeon straightened from his bow, his voice cold.
“Your Majesty, with the great undertaking nearly complete, why would you disgrace yourself like this?”
If anyone else had been there, they would have covered their eyes and ears.
Baek Yeon’s tone was far too sharp for a subject speaking to his ruler.
It was more than insolent—it was defiant.
Yet the Son of Heaven didn’t answer this time, either.
The ruler of the world gave a low laugh instead.
Only after a long while did he speak.
“The great undertaking.
Yes.
There was a great undertaking.”
“Please don’t forget the promise we made that day.”
“Forget?”
The Son of Heaven muttered with a short, incredulous laugh.
“I haven’t forgotten.
Not for a single moment since that day.”
His voice was as weak as a sick man’s.
But Baek Yeon’s eyes, fixed on the Son of Heaven, didn’t waver.
They were sunk deep and steady.
“They’ve already begun to move.
Before everything falls apart, remember that you must put things back where they belong.”
After a brief silence, the Son of Heaven nodded quietly.
He had come too far to turn back.
Once no more than the fourth prince, he now ruled all under heaven.
And he had become a man who could no longer get by without poppy.
Wasn’t it said that a horse racing across the wilderness never looked back?
Even the Son of Heaven, who stood above all people, was no exception.
He was a horse that could no longer stop of its own will.
Even if it collapsed coughing up blood, it had to keep running toward its destination.
Crack.
His hand clenched instinctively, snapping the ornate long-stemmed tobacco pipe.
The Son of Heaven stared at the broken pieces in his palm, then closed his fist tightly around them.
Thump.
The rough pieces dug into his palm.
Pain flared like a burn, and little by little, his mind began to clear.
“Ah.”
As if worshiping the heavens, the Son of Heaven tilted his head back toward the ceiling and groaned with his eyes closed.
Baek Yeon watched impassively.
“Shall I call for the imperial physician?”
“No need.
Not for an imperial physician.”
The Son of Heaven opened his eyes and continued, his voice clearer now.
“Tomorrow, I’ll meet that child in the audience hall.”
“That child would be...”
“Zhu Bao.
I wonder how much my... only younger brother has grown.”
Baek Yeon nodded.
“You can look forward to it.
He’s grown even more than Your Majesty expects.”
“Which means he’s become even more dangerous.”
Baek Yeon pressed his lips together, but the Son of Heaven understood.
All sorts of bugs gather around a tempting meal.
Now that Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao had appeared in the Imperial Capital, the enemies who resented him would surely draw the blades they had kept hidden beneath their sleeves.
Just like the nameless assassin who had come here before Baek Yeon today.
“Baek Yeon, this must never happen again.
Remember that.”
His voice was different now, cold as ice.
Baek Yeon faltered, then answered with a faint smile.
“I will engrave Your Majesty’s words into my bones.
Please forgive my disloyalty until now.”
Flutter.
In response, the Son of Heaven merely waved his sleeve.
Baek Yeon turned and began walking away.
After only a few steps, he stopped.
“And what of that man?”
“If you mean...”
“Zhu Bao.
The Murim martial artist who came with him.”
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
Baek Yeon thought carefully about the man who had suddenly come to mind.
A long while passed before he spoke.
“I don’t know.”
He had interrogated and killed tens of thousands on the battlefield, and tens of thousands more in the imperial palace.
But that was the best answer Baek Yeon could give.

paragraphs: The night Ma Sanbao came to see me, I couldn’t sleep.
It wasn’t just the rain, pouring down as if the heavens had decided to empty themselves, or the lightning crashing all around us.
My last conversation with Ma Sanbao kept replaying in my head. He’d vanished as suddenly as he’d appeared.
I need your help.
When he first said it, I couldn’t bring myself to answer.
This was a plot against the throne. There was no denying it.
If I agreed and things went wrong, no one could say what would happen afterward. With the imperial family involved, they wouldn’t treat it as one man’s wrongdoing.
I wouldn’t pay the price for failure as the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. I’d pay it as Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. That weighed heavily on me.
What happens if this fails?
You already know, don’t you?

Fail, and you’re a traitor. Succeed, and you’re the Son of Heaven. In the latter case, wealth and glory beyond anyone else’s reach await you. In the former, you’ll suffer worse than you would in hell.
I’d fought countless battles and brought down more enemies than I could count.
Some had been weak enough to handle with one finger. Others had frightened me so badly I couldn’t move a finger.
But... this was different.
The Great Nation ruled the world, and the Son of Heaven ruled the Great Nation. To rebel against the Son of Heaven meant fighting the world itself.
Not just me. Everyone around me.
Think carefully. Of course, since you set foot in the imperial palace to protect His Highness Prince Shangshan, it may already be too late.
Are you threatening me?
No. I’m telling you the truth.
Ma Sanbao, the East Depot’s second-in-command. I could still see the cold, piercing look in his eyes and hear the low voice in which he’d spoken.

How many people do you think died in the last coup? Tens of thousands were made to drink poison, died for unknown reasons on the road to exile, were torn limb from limb in the marketplace, or had their heads put on display. And those are only the deaths the world knows about. How many were never brought to light? How many of those people had nothing to do with it, just like you?
“They call it ‘calling a deer a horse.’ In the end, everything depends on the Emperor’s will. Just as a perfectly ordinary deer can become a horse, you can be made a traitor. Remember that.”
History had proven how fickle and suspicious those in power could be.
And the current Son of Heaven was undeniably a tyrant. A usurper who had defied the natural order and climbed to the throne through blood, a ruler who wielded absolute power.
Hearing Ma Sanbao say it, I began to realize what that meant.
Whether I became a traitor might already be out of my hands.
Of course, I won’t deny that I had a hand in their deaths. No—I led the way. I had to survive, whatever it took. I had to stay here and wait for the right moment.
Some had left the imperial palace to serve their young master. Others had remained to welcome him back one day.
Hong Jin was one of the former. Ma Sanbao was one of the latter.
He became the fourth prince’s—no, the new Emperor’s—hunting dog.

He was one of the cruelest of them, sinking his teeth into his targets’ necks without mercy. He survived that brutal purge and rose to become the East Depot’s second-in-command, its Brush-Holding Eunuch.
And Ma Sanbao wasn’t the only one who had survived that way.
The night we all gathered, Cang Gong said that if the East Depot had been a flower blooming in the dark until then, we had to become weeds from that day on.
Flowers were bright and beautiful whether there was light or not.
Weeds weren’t. No one spared a glance for plain, nameless grass. And because of that, it survived longer.

Cang Gong, the East Depot’s head and its Seal-Holding Eunuch, had urged his like-minded comrades to survive as weeds. He kept urging them until the illness brought on by his long years finally laid him low.
Five years ago, after Cang Gong took to his sickbed, I began leading everyone. That was when I started drawing up the pledge.
The pledge.
Clear proof that the traitors had signed their names in their own blood—and perhaps a record of the names of the meritorious officials who would one day enthrone a new Son of Heaven.
Ma Sanbao had mentioned the pledge before he left. Then he’d said something that was bound to keep me awake all night.
Dark Heaven. I know about the people throwing Murim into turmoil. Probably far more about them than you imagine, and in far greater detail.
Even if you leave now, I won’t try to stop you. But if you help us enthrone His Highness Prince Shangshan and put a new order in place... we’ll have to give you a fitting reward.
Ma Sanbao left, Hong Jin returned to the young prince’s side, and I stayed where I was, lost in thought.
Until the first light of dawn reached the window. Until the rain began to let up and day broke in the distance.
And right up to this moment.
“Fuck.”
At my sudden curse, Hyuk Mujin jolted awake from where he’d been nodding off in a corner. He sprang to his feet and fumbled for the sword in his arms, eyes still half shut.
“Are we under attack? An attack? You bastards! Who the hell dares—”
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“Go to sleep.”
“Yes.”
Hyuk Mujin flopped back down as if nothing had happened and was asleep again in no time.
The trip to the imperial capital must have been exhausting, but sleeping in that position for four whole shichen was a talent in itself.
Snore.
Still, snoring crossed the line.
Whack!
“Ugh! You bastards! No one lays a finger on the Captain!”
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“If you’re supposed to be standing guard and you sleep that soundly, they could lay hands on every part of me except one hair.”
“Gasp! Someone’s already laid a hand on you, Captain? No, you don’t have to tell me. It was Hong Jin, wasn’t it? I knew it. The way he’s always looked at you was lecherous...”
“Mujin. You little shit...!”
I groaned from the depths of my soul.
Of all people, this idiot was my right-hand man—or rather, my pinky toe.

Things were serious enough as it was, and with him like this, I’d hit a proper moment of clarity. At this point, I was starting to wonder if Dark Heaven had sent him as an ascension-to-immortality hitman to make sure I left this world early.
No System. No one I can rely on right now, either.
Thinking about it, I’d been pretty lucky until now.
The System had always pointed me toward where I needed to go, even if it did so vaguely through Quests. And whenever I wavered, Jeok Cheongang had been a sturdy pillar I could trust and lean on.
Now I had neither.
Everything that happened from here on would depend on the choice I made.
Fail, and you’re a traitor. Succeed, and you’re the Son of Heaven.
Ma Sanbao’s words echoed in my ears. So did what he’d said at the end.
Dark Heaven. I know about the people throwing Murim into turmoil. Probably far more about them than you imagine, and in far greater detail.
What exactly did he know? How had he learned so much? What connection was there between the information he’d uncovered about Dark Heaven and the Son of Heaven, and how dangerous was it?

I’d wanted to stop Ma Sanbao, who seemed determined to leave, and press him for more answers. But I held back, imagining the Embroidered Uniform Guard receiving a Buster Call and rushing over the moment I caused a commotion.
Or maybe I’d let him go because I was still trying to grasp the weight of what he’d said afterward.
Reward. A reward...
I turned the word over in my mind.
Ma Sanbao had been clear. If I helped them enthrone Prince Shangshan as the new Son of Heaven, they would give me a fitting reward.
And since he’d mentioned Dark Heaven first, it wasn’t hard to guess what he meant.
The imperial family—the Great Nation—helps the Murim Alliance wipe out Dark Heaven.
People didn’t say the government and Murim must not interfere with each other for nothing. The Great Nation had never involved itself deeply in Murim’s affairs.
No, looking at things now, the reason was obvious.
It never had a reason to.
There was no need to count the forces across the entire world. A million elite troops were stationed near the imperial capital alone, and I’d seen hundreds of Peak masters with my own eyes.
And if you included the forces that hadn’t yet come to light—especially the Supreme Peak masters...
The imperial capital alone is already far stronger than the Murim Alliance.
Of course, most of the Great Nation’s strength was concentrated there.

All the wars, including invasions by foreign peoples, had ended long ago. The emperors of a unified dynasty had no reason to give the City Lords and vassal princes scattered across the land more military power than they needed.
They had simply watched from atop those enormous, solid walls.
Watched the fierce struggle for power inside another enclosure, the one people called Murim, which stood within the Great Nation’s own borders.
Even during the Great Faction War, they had watched.
But if that Great Nation took the Murim Alliance’s side...
The scales of victory would tip in an instant.
Until now, the fight had been between the Central Plains’ Murim and Dark Heaven. If the Great Nation joined in, Dark Heaven would become an external enemy hated by all under heaven.
I still couldn’t gauge Dark Heaven’s full strength. But the weight carried by the words “Great Nation” was immense and undeniable.
There was, of course, one fatal problem.
What if we failed?
High risk. High reward.
Fail, and you’re a traitor. Succeed, and you’re the Son of Heaven.
I felt as though I were standing at the edge of a cliff.
I could gain the Son of Heaven’s wings and soar above the clouds. Or the Son of Heaven could break both my legs and send me tumbling over the edge.
Not just me. Everyone.
Snore.
Right. Including this idiot.
“...Mujin. You little shit.”
Hyuk Mujin opened his eyes naturally and spoke.
“I wasn’t asleep.”
“Is that so?”
“Yes.”
“Then why were you snoring so damn loud? The Embroidered Uniform Guard will be up here to haul you away soon. Your snoring woke the Emperor.”
“I’m serious.”
“How are you going to prove it?”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes darted around before he answered.
“I’ll stake Hong Jin’s balls on it.”
This idiot was trying to stake something that didn’t exist.
Before I could think of a reply, a familiar metallic sound came from outside the window.
Clack. Clack.
Orderly movement. A sharp aura.
The Embroidered Uniform Guard.
Hyuk Mujin stared at the golden-armored guards entering the pavilion and asked, wide-eyed,
“Did the Emperor really wake up because of me?”
Should I really kill him?
I let out a deep sigh.
“Go bring His Highness Prince Shangshan.”
It looked like the time had come.
