chapters.title: Chapter 874
paragraphs: Perhaps the outcome had been decided long ago.
The imperial palace, a perfect enemy stronghold. A guard so tight that even “ironclad” didn’t do it justice. And the Emperor, ruler of all under heaven.
He had taken charge of the stage, the actors, and the direction himself. Even if a character like me stepped into the scene, it probably wouldn’t change much.
A thought struck me.
Perhaps all of this was a kind of amusement to the Emperor.
Why else summon me along with Prince Shangshan when he had no need to see me? Why brush aside words that could have gotten me branded a traitor on the spot?
And why look at my rigid face now and sneer?
Crack.
A bone shifted with a sound from my tightly clenched fist. I scanned the impassive eyes visible above the assassins’ pitch-black masks, weighing my options.
What do I do?
The Emperor’s little game was daring—and supremely confident.
Naturally, everyone in our party had been forced to surrender their weapons on entering the palace. But beyond that, no restrictions had been placed on me.
Perhaps he was confident that no one under heaven could harm him.
If so, he’d made a clear mistake.
Even barehanded, I was a superhuman who had opened my Middle Dantian, an heir to the Fire Gate Clan who had inherited the Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s fearsome fist and palm techniques.
All I have to do is take their weapons.
With every shift of my gaze, a path invisible to anyone else took shape in my mind.
A path to kill the assassins as quickly and efficiently as possible, then escape with Prince Shangshan.
The fact that the Emperor was a master who had entered the realm of Supreme Peak was unexpected, but that was all.
He’s only just entered Supreme Peak. What if I’m willing to sacrifice an arm to capture him first?
If I took the Emperor hostage, it would all be over. The Great Nation was one enormous mechanism, and the Emperor was both its master and its most important part.
With him in my hands, I could neutralize not only the assassins in here but also the twin masters waiting outside.
Perhaps even Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
But... what then? What happens after that?
Once I started, there would be no going back. That would be the beginning of a true rebellion.

If I took the Emperor hostage and fled Qianqing Palace, would the East Depot, led by Ma Sanbao, help us? Were the people who had signed the collective pledge he’d mentioned the night before fully prepared?
As thoughts tangled through my mind—
“Your servant, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao, will obey the will of my most august elder brother, Your Majesty.”
Prince Shangshan bowed deeply before his one and only elder brother—the Emperor, who stood above all others—and cried out at the top of his voice.
“Long live the Emperor! Long live the Emperor! Long, long live the Emperor!”
My heart lurched.
Was it because Prince Shangshan’s sudden action had broken the tension gripping my whole body?
No.
It was because I could read the desperate plea in that young prince, so small he didn’t even reach my chest.
Don’t step in any further.
It was as if a voice I couldn’t hear, a voice that couldn’t be heard, had sounded in my ear.
Prince Shangshan was trying to stop me. He had stepped forward before I could make a choice that couldn’t be undone.
The Emperor looked down at him with an arrogant gaze.
“...You’ve certainly grown.”
He murmured it with an unreadable expression, then swept his sleeve. Prince Shangshan, who had been crying “Long live” and bowing again and again, understood the gesture and rose.
“Do you truly intend to obey my will?”
“Of course, Your Majesty.”
“That sounds as though it isn’t your own will. You may refuse if you don’t want to.”
That was what he said, but his narrowed eyes suggested otherwise.
Prince Shangshan lowered his head without a word. Unlike before, his answer was perfectly calm.
“It is my will, too.”
“I’m overjoyed that we brothers are of one mind.”
“I am deeply honored.”
Prince Shangshan seemed to have accepted what was happening. At the sight of his calm face, the tension drained out of me. I steadied my breathing.
It’s no good.
Prince Shangshan had made the right choice.
The answer was clear. We had to retreat when we weren’t prepared.
At least for today.
The Emperor watched me and smacked his lips, then suddenly spoke.
“Now that you’ve decided, there’s no need for further discussion. This audience is over. Everyone, withdraw.”
“As Your Majesty commands.”
The assassins hoisted Third Shadow’s body onto their backs and melted into the darkness. Then the Emperor added,
“No Shadow. You too.”
Shff.
The air rippled in answer. I barely held back a groan.
This is insane.
A Supreme Peak master whose presence even I hadn’t sensed.
No—a Supreme Peak assassin.
That was probably why the Emperor had been so untroubled about letting me into his chambers without imposing any serious restrictions.
He’d been testing me to the very end.
I revised my judgment of the Emperor at once.
He wasn’t merely arrogant and daring. He was more meticulous and suspicious than anyone.
If you succeed, you’re the Emperor. If you fail, you’re a traitor.
I hadn’t thought far enough ahead. When he was still known as the Fourth Prince, he had drawn his sword, swung it once, and overturned the Imperial Capital to seize the Great Nation.
Such boldness and decisiveness were beyond anything an ordinary person could dream of.
The thought suddenly crossed my mind: if I’d made a move, I would never have left Qianqing Palace alive.
Damn it.
Was this the power of the Emperor? The power of the Great Nation?
Was my best option really to withdraw so helplessly, unable even to protect a young prince?
“Let’s go.”
At Prince Shangshan’s quiet murmur, I turned away to hide my gritted teeth.
The Emperor had finished his game and vanished behind the fluttering silks.
Rumble.
A massive iron door, out of place in such a splendid chamber, slowly opened. Beyond it stood dozens of palace attendants I hadn’t seen on the way in.
“We greet His Highness Prince Shangshan.”
“We greet His Highness Prince Shangshan.”
They bowed to Prince Shangshan with utmost deference. Every one of them was a striking beauty.
Each had the kind of looks said to topple kingdoms.
But one woman standing a step ahead of the rest caught my eye at once.
“Please call me So Gyo.”
So Gyo. That was her name.
Her voice was calm, and her eyes shone like the morning star. Even apart from her beautiful features, there was something unusual about her.
“By His Majesty’s solemn command, we have been assigned to serve His Highness Prince Shangshan. We humble women will attend to you from now on, so please do not worry.”
It was simple enough to understand why none of the people assigned to accompany the prince were heavily armed Embroidered Uniform Guards.
They’ve trained in martial arts. And to a considerable level, too.
Every one of them had the internal energy of a First Rate master.
I also recognized the thin belts at their waists for what they were: flexible swords.
And I couldn’t help guessing that if the Emperor gave the order, they’d be ready to drive those blades into Prince Shangshan’s neck at any moment.
There’s no time.
I was getting anxious. I had to meet Hong Jin as soon as possible and make a plan. I had to see through the Emperor’s hidden intentions, to discern his scheme.
“Your Highness.”
Prince Shangshan lifted his head at my call. He looked at me with calm eyes. Whether that calm came from composure or resignation, I couldn’t tell. Then he turned to So Gyo.
“I’d like you to give us a moment.”
Working as a palace attendant in Qianqing Palace meant that they, too, were among the Emperor’s many loyal servants.
But after a moment’s thought, So Gyo quietly led the others away through the maze of corridors.
Only then did Prince Shangshan manage a smile.
“Speak. Though we may not meet again for some time, understand that the circumstances aren’t right for a long farewell.”
There was something about a child who had grown up too soon that brought a lump to your throat.
But I couldn’t let my emotions take over.
I swallowed the words rising to my throat and held out my hand.
“First, take this.”
“Come on. There’s no time.”
Prince Shangshan hesitated, then took what I offered. When he saw the small, glimmering object in his palm, his eyes widened.
“This is...”
“A gift from me.”
He examined it curiously.
“It’s the ring you always wear.”
Prince Shangshan couldn’t know or even guess its proper name: the Myriad-Poison Ring.
A divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan, and one of the divine weapons Dark Heaven had targeted.
Unlike White Flame and Fire Dragon Armor, which I usually kept in my Inventory, this was a ring I always wore, just in case.
“Why would you suddenly give this to me?”
“I thought you might need it, Your Highness. You looked at it with interest several times on the way to the Imperial Capital.”
It was true. We’d spent a long time in the carriage, and Prince Shangshan had taken an interest in everything I owned.
Even this ring, too clunky for the women of this era and awkward for a man to wear.
A few days ago, he’d even pestered me to give it to him.
“About that ring.”
“Hm? Oh, this one?”
“Yes. The one you’re wearing. Would you give it to me?”
“Um, sorry, but that’s a little difficult. Have you always been interested in accessories?”
“No. I just want something of yours.”
“Oh, collecting keepsakes...”
“What was that?”
“Nothing. Just talking to myself.”
“At any rate, I’d like to have it. Of course, I’ll pay you handsomely.”
“I’m sorry. I can’t give this to anyone, and I couldn’t sell it for any amount of money.”
“Why not? Is it so precious that you’d refuse even my request?”
“Well, you see... Right. It was my father’s keepsake.”
“Oh.”
“It means a lot not just to me, but to the whole family. My eldest brother still cries whenever he sees this ring.”
“I believe your father is still alive.”
“...Now that you mention it, I think it was my mother’s keepsake. I was mistaken.”
The Myriad-Poison Ring was never supposed to end up in anyone else’s hands.
In the end, Prince Shangshan had been disappointed, and I’d promised to sign about five thousand autographs when we returned to Shanxi Province.
Back then, I hadn’t had the faintest idea what awaited us in the Imperial Capital.
“Are you really giving this to me?”
“Not for good. You have to return it later.”
“Didn’t you say it was your mother’s keepsake?”
“Uh. Well, you see...”
Just as I ran out of things to say, Prince Shangshan let out a quiet laugh.
“I already know you were lying.”
“Ah.”
“I’m a little disappointed that you’d lie even to me, but it’s all right. You must have had your reasons. It must be that precious.”
I smiled along with him.
“That’s right. It’s very precious, so always keep it where no one else can see it...and make sure you return it.”
He was an old soul in a child’s body. He understood what I meant.
Prince Shangshan hesitated as though he didn’t know what to say, then nodded firmly.
“Mm. I understand. I promise.”
Only then did I feel a little more at ease.
The Emperor had seized the throne through a coup more than a decade ago, earning countless enemies in the shadows and no shortage of condemnation.

The Emperor cared enough about having a legitimate pretext to summon Prince Shangshan to the Imperial Capital before bringing him under his control. If he meant to kill his one and only younger brother, the most likely method was poison.
As long as Prince Shangshan keeps the Myriad-Poison Ring on him, poisoning him won’t be an option.
That would buy me time to find another way.
As I thought it over, I sensed the palace attendants slowly returning from farther down the corridor.
Our brief farewell was almost over.
“It’s time for me to go,” Prince Shangshan murmured, his voice subdued.
I bent down to meet his eyes.
“We’ll meet again soon.”
“I hope so. Then I’ll be able to repay the debt I owe you.”
“Your Highness.”
“Yes?”
“Don’t you know? Friends don’t owe each other anything.”
“Still, if you insist on giving me something, I’ll accept it gratefully.”
I grinned and ruffled Prince Shangshan’s hair.
The young prince stared blankly at me with wide eyes, then smiled, too.

chapters.title: Chapter 875
paragraphs: The farewell was brief.
Before long, the palace attendants returned. They surrounded Prince Shangshan and led him away through Qianqing Palace’s vast, maze-like corridors.
For now, this is the best I can do.
I thought to myself as I watched the young prince’s back, glimpsed now and then between the attendants.
How much time did that child have left?
I didn’t know.
If I’d gained anything from this audience, it was confirmation that the Emperor wasn’t a complete madman who would stop at nothing.
His coup has already made him plenty of enemies. He can’t get rid of his youngest brother the same way.
Everything needs at least some pretext.

Even in an era of absolute monarchy, with the Emperor ruling over all, that was no exception. And the Emperor, who’d brought a bloody storm to the imperial palace more than a decade ago, had dangers lurking out of sight.
Old retainers who longed for the late Emperor.
And common people who pitied the young prince.
If Prince Shangshan died under unnatural circumstances now, it would give someone a pretext for another rebellion.
Poisoning would look the most natural...but it won’t be easy.
No one knew exactly how far the Myriad-Poison Ring’s power extended.

But it was a rare treasure that had even absorbed the Formless Ultimate Poison that once spread through Jeok Cheongang’s body. Even the Emperor wouldn’t have an easy time obtaining poison of that caliber.
Unless he eventually discovered the Myriad-Poison Ring and took it by force.
But I’ve bought us some time, at least.
Did I regret leaving the Myriad-Poison Ring with Prince Shangshan?
No.
From everything I’d seen so far, the Emperor and Dark Heaven were definitely connected somehow, and if the imperial family fell into their hands, it was all over.
I had to protect Prince Shangshan, even at the risk of losing the ring.
He was the anti-Emperor faction’s only hope, the one person who could hold it together.
And he was one of the friends I’d made here.
Though there’s a bit of an age gap for me to call him a friend.
I smiled bitterly and watched until Prince Shangshan and his party disappeared from sight.
When I turned away, heavy-hearted, a woman stood quietly watching me. I still wasn’t used to seeing her, but her face was the sort I’d remember for a long time after a single meeting.
“Have you been waiting long?”
So Gyo answered calmly. “No. This humble woman is carrying out His Majesty the Emperor’s orders. What does it matter whether the wait is long or short?”
Can’t fault her loyalty.
I gave an awkward nod. “Then let’s go.”
The Emperor’s order So Gyo had mentioned was to guide me out of Qianqing Palace.
Of course, “guide” was a polite way of saying she was watching me and kicking me out. But what did it matter?
“I’ll lead the way. Please follow me.”
I’d barely taken a few steps after her when I frowned.
“Wait. I don’t think this is the right way.”
“It is. You remember the way we came.”
Of course I did. I’d made a point of checking my escape route in case the worst happened.
“Don’t just say it is. I’m telling you we’re going the wrong way.”
“The way into Qianqing Palace is different from the way out.”
“What?”

“The life gate can become the death gate, and the death gate can become the life gate. Since you’re a martial artist who travels the martial world, Young Master Jin, I thought you would understand what that means.”
I fell silent. A word flashed through my mind like a bolt of lightning.
“Don’t tell me...mechanisms and formations?”
So Gyo gave a slight nod and started walking again. I stared after her for a moment before hurrying to follow, still reeling from what she’d told me.
Damn it. Even for an Emperor, this is ridiculous. This isn’t a residence. It’s an impregnable fortress.
There were no fewer than three Supreme Peak masters stationed in Qianqing Palace, not counting the Emperor.
One was a master of the concealment technique who guarded him at close range. And even by a conservative estimate, more than a hundred elite assassins were stationed throughout the palace.
On top of all that, mechanisms and formations?
He’s definitely not normal.
Naturally, an Emperor needed tight security. But there were limits.
The defenses here were abnormal, as though they reflected the Emperor I’d met just moments ago.
Maybe he was afraid, too. He made so many enemies.
They said thirty thousand people had been dismembered or beheaded during his coup.
Among them were his own blood relatives in the imperial family, founding heroes who had laid the foundations of the Great Nation, upright officials, and renowned scholars.
All of them had died.
Killed in a coup that defied the natural order, on the command of a single man.
It would have been absurd if an Emperor like that didn’t have enemies.
Then could it be...?
As I followed So Gyo, I thought of him not as the Emperor who stood above all others, but as a Supreme Peak master.
His formidable martial prowess. His face, which looked ten years older than it should have—no, a good twenty years older for a man so young and so skilled.
Was that why?
Supreme Peak was a lofty realm no one could enter through innate talent alone.
And yet the ruler of the continent, who had everything anyone could want, had sweated blood to learn martial arts.
He must have swung weapons without pause, like the martial artists of the martial world he called ruffians. At times, he must have groaned under pain that racked his whole body.
Even so, it seemed he had never entirely shaken his fear of assassination or his nightmares.
It’s only a guess, but it’s certainly possible.
I’d taken countless lives with these hands. I thought I could understand a little of what he felt.
There was no such thing as a justifiable killing. Only a killing with a pretext.
I’d comforted myself by saying I’d had no choice, that they were people I had to defeat. But that didn’t change the truth.
The countless dead would come to torment me from time to time—maybe even quite often—and I’d wake up drenched in cold sweat.
So what must it be like for an Emperor who’d killed tens of thousands in a coup with no pretext at all?
His nights must be a real inferno.
I smiled bitterly and kept walking. So Gyo led me onward without a word, deeper into passages I couldn’t make sense of.
I was starting to get a bad feeling.
“Um, can I ask you something?”
So Gyo stopped and turned around. At the same time, she spoke without hesitation.
“It’s all right.”
“What?”
“I mean that nothing unfortunate will happen to you, Young Master Jin. Please follow me.”
I was quiet for a moment, then clicked my tongue.
“Right to the heart of it. Did you learn to read minds?”
“No. I noticed that your breathing had become slightly uneven.”
“Oh. I gave it away, huh? You’re perceptive.”
“I’ve learned martial arts as well. Few things matter more to a martial artist than controlling one’s breathing.”
She was right. The higher a master’s realm, the more likely a fight was to be decided in less than a breath.
But that didn’t change how pointed she sounded. As I watched her turn away, I thought, Is she picking a fight with me?
Probably. No, almost certainly.
It was absurd for So Gyo, who was First Rate at best, to lecture me. I let it pass with a silent chuckle.
She was one of the Emperor’s loyal servants, and I was in enemy territory. What else could I expect?
I should be grateful she isn’t attacking me.
There was no point arguing. I shook my head and was about to start walking again when—
Crash.
The sound was faint, but I heard it clearly. It came from somewhere in a dark corridor beyond one of the paths branching off like a crossroads.
Then I heard an irritated voice.
“You lowly wretches! How dare you...!”
“Please follow me.”
So Gyo hurried over and blocked my path. Ignoring her, I drew up my internal energy and sharpened my senses.
A woman. That was definitely a woman’s voice.
Something was going on. Something I didn’t know about yet.
And if I wanted to accomplish what I’d come to do in this damn imperial palace, I needed every clue I could get.
Step.
“Young Master Jin!”
Her low shout reached me the moment I stepped toward the darkness. She glared at me, her cold eyes carrying an unmistakable warning.
That only made me more certain. If she was this determined to stop me, there was something outsiders must never see.
But this was the Emperor’s residence. I put on an innocent smile and pretended not to understand.
“It sounded like something happened. Shouldn’t we go take a look?”
“I told you to follow me.”
“Come on. The imperial palace isn’t very friendly, is it? Who was that just now? Sounded like a woman to me.”
“That’s enough. I’ve warned you.”

Shhk-shhk-shhk!

Black masks as dark as the shadows, with the eyes of killers visible above them.

So Gyo put a hand on the flexible sword at her waist. “It won’t. As long as you turn around and leave quietly.”

Ssshhh.

“Fine. I surrender.”

I’d heard that woman’s sharp cry clearly.

Right. Aehyang.
The beloved concubine the Emperor had taken from the City Lord of Sichuan Province.

sentences.text: The farewell was brief.
Before long, the palace attendants returned.
They surrounded Prince Shangshan and led him away through Qianqing Palace’s vast, maze-like corridors.
For now, this is the best I can do.
I thought to myself as I watched the young prince’s back, glimpsed now and then between the attendants.
How much time did that child have left?
I didn’t know.
If I’d gained anything from this audience, it was confirmation that the Emperor wasn’t a complete madman who would stop at nothing.
His coup has already made him plenty of enemies.
He can’t get rid of his youngest brother the same way.
Everything needs at least some pretext.
Even in an era of absolute monarchy, with the Emperor ruling over all, that was no exception.
And the Emperor, who’d brought a bloody storm to the imperial palace more than a decade ago, had dangers lurking out of sight.
Old retainers who longed for the late Emperor.
And common people who pitied the young prince.
If Prince Shangshan died under unnatural circumstances now, it would give someone a pretext for another rebellion.
Poisoning would look the most natural...but it won’t be easy.
No one knew exactly how far the Myriad-Poison Ring’s power extended.
But it was a rare treasure that had even absorbed the Formless Ultimate Poison that once spread through Jeok Cheongang’s body.
Even the Emperor wouldn’t have an easy time obtaining poison of that caliber.
Unless he eventually discovered the Myriad-Poison Ring and took it by force.
But I’ve bought us some time, at least.
Did I regret leaving the Myriad-Poison Ring with Prince Shangshan?
No.
From everything I’d seen so far, the Emperor and Dark Heaven were definitely connected somehow, and if the imperial family fell into their hands, it was all over.
I had to protect Prince Shangshan, even at the risk of losing the ring.
He was the anti-Emperor faction’s only hope, the one person who could hold it together.
And he was one of the friends I’d made here.
Though there’s a bit of an age gap for me to call him a friend.
I smiled bitterly and watched until Prince Shangshan and his party disappeared from sight.
When I turned away, heavy-hearted, a woman stood quietly watching me.
I still wasn’t used to seeing her, but her face was the sort I’d remember for a long time after a single meeting.
“Have you been waiting long?”
So Gyo answered calmly.
“No.
This humble woman is carrying out His Majesty the Emperor’s orders.
What does it matter whether the wait is long or short?”
Can’t fault her loyalty.
I gave an awkward nod.
“Then let’s go.”
The Emperor’s order So Gyo had mentioned was to guide me out of Qianqing Palace.
Of course, “guide” was a polite way of saying she was watching me and kicking me out.
But what did it matter?
“I’ll lead the way.
Please follow me.”
I’d barely taken a few steps after her when I frowned.
“Wait.
I don’t think this is the right way.”
“It is.
You remember the way we came.”
Of course I did.
I’d made a point of checking my escape route in case the worst happened.
“Don’t just say it is.
I’m telling you we’re going the wrong way.”
“The way into Qianqing Palace is different from the way out.”
“What?”
“The life gate can become the death gate, and the death gate can become the life gate.
Since you’re a martial artist who travels the martial world, Young Master Jin, I thought you would understand what that means.”
I fell silent.
A word flashed through my mind like a bolt of lightning.
“Don’t tell me...mechanisms and formations?”
So Gyo gave a slight nod and started walking again.
I stared after her for a moment before hurrying to follow, still reeling from what she’d told me.
Damn it.
Even for an Emperor, this is ridiculous.
This isn’t a residence.
It’s an impregnable fortress.
There were no fewer than three Supreme Peak masters stationed in Qianqing Palace, not counting the Emperor.
One was a master of the concealment technique who guarded him at close range.
And even by a conservative estimate, more than a hundred elite assassins were stationed throughout the palace.
On top of all that, mechanisms and formations?
He’s definitely not normal.
Naturally, an Emperor needed tight security.
But there were limits.
The defenses here were abnormal, as though they reflected the Emperor I’d met just moments ago.
Maybe he was afraid, too.
He made so many enemies.
They said thirty thousand people had been dismembered or beheaded during his coup.
Among them were his own blood relatives in the imperial family, founding heroes who had laid the foundations of the Great Nation, upright officials, and renowned scholars.
All of them had died.
Killed in a coup that defied the natural order, on the command of a single man.
It would have been absurd if an Emperor like that didn’t have enemies.
Then could it be...?
As I followed So Gyo, I thought of him not as the Emperor who stood above all others, but as a Supreme Peak master.
His formidable martial prowess.
His face, which looked ten years older than it should have—no, a good twenty years older for a man so young and so skilled.
Was that why?
Supreme Peak was a lofty realm no one could enter through innate talent alone.
And yet the ruler of the continent, who had everything anyone could want, had sweated blood to learn martial arts.
He must have swung weapons without pause, like the martial artists of the martial world he called ruffians.
At times, he must have groaned under pain that racked his whole body.
Even so, it seemed he had never entirely shaken his fear of assassination or his nightmares.
It’s only a guess, but it’s certainly possible.
I’d taken countless lives with these hands.
I thought I could understand a little of what he felt.
There was no such thing as a justifiable killing.
Only a killing with a pretext.
I’d comforted myself by saying I’d had no choice, that they were people I had to defeat.
But that didn’t change the truth.
The countless dead would come to torment me from time to time—maybe even quite often—and I’d wake up drenched in cold sweat.
So what must it be like for an Emperor who’d killed tens of thousands in a coup with no pretext at all?
His nights must be a real inferno.
I smiled bitterly and kept walking.
So Gyo led me onward without a word, deeper into passages I couldn’t make sense of.
I was starting to get a bad feeling.
“Um, can I ask you something?”
So Gyo stopped and turned around.
At the same time, she spoke without hesitation.
“It’s all right.”
“What?”
“I mean that nothing unfortunate will happen to you, Young Master Jin.
Please follow me.”
I was quiet for a moment, then clicked my tongue.
“Right to the heart of it.
Did you learn to read minds?”
“No.
I noticed that your breathing had become slightly uneven.”
“Oh.
I gave it away, huh?
You’re perceptive.”
“I’ve learned martial arts as well.

She was right.
The higher a master’s realm, the more likely a fight was to be decided in less than a breath.
But that didn’t change how pointed she sounded.
As I watched her turn away, I thought, Is she picking a fight with me?
Probably.
No, almost certainly.
It was absurd for So Gyo, who was First Rate at best, to lecture me.
I let it pass with a silent chuckle.
She was one of the Emperor’s loyal servants, and I was in enemy territory.
What else could I expect?
I should be grateful she isn’t attacking me.
There was no point arguing.

Crash.
The sound was faint, but I heard it clearly.

A woman.

Something was going on.

chapters.title: Chapter 876
paragraphs: Hong Jin stared hard at the golden armor blocking his way.
His voice, usually as high and gentle as a woman’s, had sunk lower than anyone had ever heard it.
“Move.”
“Impossible. You cannot take a single step beyond this place.”
“I said move.”
“Sir! Deputy Military Commissioner!”
“Do you really think you can stop me? You lot dare?”
The several dozen Embroidered Uniform Guards looked at one another, their faces stiff.
They already knew the eunuch standing before them was no pushover.

They said no matter how high you climbed, power never lasted ten years, and no flower stayed red for ten days. But things were different when you were talking about the East Depot’s former Investigating Eunuch, who had once enjoyed the late Emperor’s favor.
Besides, plenty of old officials still remained at court, and Hong Jin surely had ties with them.
Whether those ties were friendships forged as fellow servants of the late Emperor or secrets he’d seized while holding sway over the East Depot, no one could say. But one thing was certain.
His influence was not to be underestimated.

“Even after more than ten years away from the palace, a few letters are enough to send a low-ranking Embroidered Uniform Guard to the borderlands. So get the hell out of my way, if you want to keep wearing that shiny armor.”
A cold flame flickered in Hong Jin’s eyes.
It had been two shichen since his young lord left to meet the Emperor.
The eunuch, renowned even within the East Depot for his cool head, was already at the end of his patience.
If I’d known it would come to this, I should’ve done whatever it took to go with him.
Something had clearly happened.
He tried to suppress the unease that kept rising inside him, but even that was getting harder to do.
Just as Hong Jin bit down hard on his lip without realizing it—
“Everyone, calm down. Take it easy.”
A breezy voice cut in out of nowhere. Hyuk Mujin stepped in front of Hong Jin and waved the Embroidered Uniform Guards down.
“Try to be understanding. It’s taking a while, so he’s worried.”
“Martial artist Hyuk!”
“Come now, Comrade Hong, you should calm down too. What did these people do wrong? We underlings do what we’re told, whether they say ‘get down’ or ‘bark.’ Right?”
The Embroidered Uniform Guards frowned, unsure whether he was taking their side or calling them sons of bitches to their faces. Hyuk Mujin didn’t give them time to think it over.
“Still, could you at least find out what’s going on? We’re tired enough as it is. If you make this difficult, nobody’s going to have a good time. Right?”
“Wait. That’s...”

“Oh, you’ll check? Wow! The Embroidered Uniform Guard! The pride of the Great Nation! The guardians of the imperial family! Thanks a fucking lot! If you get the time, drop by the Hyuk Family Textile Shop in the center of the Imperial Capital. Give them my name and you can get a discount.”
There was no chance to reply. Without waiting for the guards’ answer, Hyuk Mujin turned, grabbed Hong Jin, and hurried him away.
He spoke in a low whisper.
“There’s nothing to gain by provoking them right now. You know better than most, so why are you doing this? Get a grip.”
Those words didn’t make Hong Jin’s unease disappear, but they were enough to remind him of the reality he’d briefly forgotten.
Hyuk Mujin was right.
If he used his remaining influence at court to move a few powerful figures, all he’d manage to do was get rid of a few hunting dogs.
He wouldn’t touch the body, let alone the head. Reaching the owner holding the hunting dogs’ leashes was out of the question.
Now was the time to hide his claws and sheath his fangs.
Of course, though his head had cooled, his heart was still pounding wildly.
“Aren’t you worried, Martial artist Hyuk?”
At Hong Jin’s sudden question, Hyuk Mujin tilted his head.
“Sorry? About what?”
“You don’t feel any particular loyalty toward His Highness Prince Shangshan. I know that. It’s the nature of martial artists, so I have no intention of criticizing you for it. But...”
“Oh, you mean I’m not worried about what happened to the Captain who went with him?”
Hong Jin nodded weakly, and Hyuk Mujin answered at once.
“Of course I’m worried. I am.”
“Then how can you be so calm?”
“This is the best I can do.”
“What?”
“I’ve followed the Captain through all kinds of trouble. Whenever he’s stepped in to handle something himself, he’s found a way to settle it.”

“No matter how badly things got tangled, in the end, the Captain swept it all away. All those bastards who strutted around claiming to be masters or secret masterminds went off to interview with Yama.”
Hyuk Mujin looked at Hong Jin’s wide eyes and continued in an unruffled voice.
“To be perfectly honest, I’ve never met anyone as strong as the Captain. He’s insanely strong.”
“Martial artist Hyuk, I’m sorry, but I’ll be blunt. The imperial palace is practically a living monster. No matter how skilled a Supreme Peak master Young Master Jin is...”
“I wasn’t just talking about martial arts.”
“Not his martial arts. The man himself. He’s just a strong person, period. That’s the kind of person the Captain is.”
“Even if the palace is crawling with masters a level or two above him, they still won’t be able to handle the Captain. It makes no sense, but that’s how the Captain I know has always been.”
“Does that make any sense?”
“It shouldn’t, but somehow it does. Isn’t that why you asked our Captain to look after His Highness Prince Shangshan?”
Hong Jin was struck speechless. Then he understood.
When he’d first received Ma Sanbao’s secret letter saying the Embroidered Uniform Guard was on the move, why had Jin Taekyung been the first person to come to mind?
Trust between them?
Of course that mattered. But if trust alone had been the deciding factor, he would have brought Li Feng, a lay disciple of Huashan and the Assistant Military Commissioner of Shanxi Province.
Though Li Feng and Hong Jin had briefly been at odds, Li Feng had remained unwaveringly loyal to Prince Shangshan for years, even when the prince had been all but cast adrift.
Compared to that, calling Hong Jin’s relationship with Jin Taekyung one of mutual trust was a little embarrassing.
It was true that he had a fairly close business relationship with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
But why?
Why had he asked for Jin Taekyung when he could have brought a proven loyalist or another master from the martial world?
Hong Jin already knew the answer.
“You’re right, Martial artist Hyuk. I’d foolishly forgotten for a moment. I let my emotions get the better of me.”
Seeing Hong Jin regain his composure as if nothing had happened, Hyuk Mujin grinned.
“I understand. It happens.”

“Young Master Jin... yes, he really is an unfathomable person. Most of what I’ve heard about him is hard to believe. Of course, some of the information I went to great trouble to obtain must be nonsense.”
“Nonsense? What information?”
“Oh, that?”
Hong Jin gave a small laugh.
“You’d laugh your head off if you heard it, too, Martial artist Hyuk. Apparently, Young Master Jin caught a dragon in Dongting Lake.”
“That’s definitely a rumor. It was more of an imugi than a dragon.”
“Thought so. I paid a thousand gold pieces for that information, and this is the kind of ridiculous...”
Hong Jin stopped mid-sentence.
After a breathless silence, he finally managed to squeeze out a few words.
“What did you just say?”
“Huh? What do you mean?”
“No, just now. You said it wasn’t a dragon...”

“Oh. An imugi. That’s right. I was there, too. At first I thought I was dreaming, but after a while I realized I wasn’t. Well, it didn’t fly through the sky, so it definitely wasn’t a dragon. It was an imugi.”
“By the way, what piece of shit leaked that information? That was supposed to have been handled quietly, under the strictest secrecy.”
Still reeling as if time had stopped, Hong Jin realized that everything Hyuk Mujin had said earlier had been true. Every last word.
Choosing Jin Taekyung really had been a stroke of genius.
An imugi? He caught an imugi? A person caught an imugi? Wait, those things actually exist?
The shock was so great that, for a moment, he even forgot to worry about the young prince.
Just as Hong Jin stood frozen with his mouth hanging open, Hyuk Mujin, who’d been cursing the rumor-monger for some time, cautiously spoke up.
“Um, would you be willing to spend another thousand gold pieces? I saw a talking tiger when I went to Nanman recently...”
“Move!”
A shout rang out, carried on internal energy. It was a voice Hong Jin knew all too well.
Hong Jin whipped his head around. His eyes widened like saucers when he saw who it was, while Hyuk Mujin, who’d been trying to strike a quiet deal, cried out on instinct.
“I’m sorry! Please spare me! I didn’t say anything! May the Captain protect me—long live the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
“I’m back. I have something to tell you, so let’s get inside... Hyuk Mujin, you little shit, what’s wrong with you? Why is he acting like that?”
Hong Jin had been about to tell him about the talking tiger, but his heart sank.
Where is His Highness...?
No matter how many times he looked around, he couldn’t see him.
His young lord. The Great Nation’s last hope.
Hong Jin rubbed his eyes with his sleeve again and again, but only one person was coming toward him.
Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
So it’s come to this.
Something had definitely happened. That cruel Emperor’s hand had finally reached his lord.
But Hong Jin fought back the haze gathering before his eyes.
It wasn’t over yet. Surely that young martial artist had found some way out.
And as if to answer Hong Jin’s hopes, Jin Taekyung—who’d nearly knocked the Embroidered Uniform Guards, standing firm as iron towers, flying with a shoulder-check—moved his lips.
“Get inside the pavilion. Right now!”
Of course, he didn’t forget to smack his one loyal subordinate on the back of the head in the moment he had to spare.
“Glad you returned safely...”
Whack!
“Ow!”
“Yeah, I’m back safe and sound, you little shit.”
Back at the pavilion, I used my internal energy to soundproof the place, then quickly laid out what had happened.
As briefly as possible. Just the essentials.
First. The Emperor had locked Prince Shangshan inside Qianqing Palace under the pretext of protecting him.

Second. That Emperor was shameless as hell. Like the rabbit in the old folktale who left his liver behind, he seemed to keep his conscience hidden somewhere else. Oh, and he was a Supreme Peak master who looked way older than he was.
Third. It seemed like the beloved concubine the Emperor had taken from the City Lord of Sichuan Province a few months ago was in Qianqing Palace.

That wrapped up my summary. Even the twenty-first-century summary junkies who treated their eyes and scroll wheels as mere decorations would’ve given it a passing grade. Hong Jin’s expression had changed with every point; now all that remained was unconcealable shock.
“The City Lord of Sichuan Province’s concubine... is staying in Qianqing Palace?”
“Yes. Almost certainly. But before I draw my own conclusions, there’s something I need to ask you.”
I took a deep breath and asked again.
“Is it normal for the Empress or the imperial consorts to stay in Qianqing Palace?”
“Not at all.”
“Even a consort the Emperor favors?”
“Not at all. The rules of the imperial family are strict.”
“Then...”
“That’s right. There’s only one explanation.”
Hong Jin and I met eyes. The next moment, we spoke at the same time.
“Pregnant.”
“With child.”
Fuck.
The Emperor seemed to have found a new heir for the Great Nation to replace Prince Shangshan.

“It shouldn’t, but somehow it does.
Isn’t that why you asked our Captain to look after His Highness Prince Shangshan?”
Hong Jin was struck speechless.
Then he understood.
When he’d first received Ma Sanbao’s secret letter saying the Embroidered Uniform Guard was on the move, why had Jin Taekyung been the first person to come to mind?
Trust between them?
Of course that mattered.
But if trust alone had been the deciding factor, he would have brought Li Feng, a lay disciple of Huashan and the Assistant Military Commissioner of Shanxi Province.
Though Li Feng and Hong Jin had briefly been at odds, Li Feng had remained unwaveringly loyal to Prince Shangshan for years, even when the prince had been all but cast adrift.
Compared to that, calling Hong Jin’s relationship with Jin Taekyung one of mutual trust was a little embarrassing.
It was true that he had a fairly close business relationship with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
But why?
Why had he asked for Jin Taekyung when he could have brought a proven loyalist or another master from the martial world?
Hong Jin already knew the answer.
“You’re right, Martial artist Hyuk.
I’d foolishly forgotten for a moment.
I let my emotions get the better of me.”
Seeing Hong Jin regain his composure as if nothing had happened, Hyuk Mujin grinned.
“I understand.
It happens.”
“Young Master Jin... yes, he really is an unfathomable person.
Most of what I’ve heard about him is hard to believe.
Of course, some of the information I went to great trouble to obtain must be nonsense.”
“Nonsense?
What information?”
“Oh, that?”
Hong Jin gave a small laugh.
“You’d laugh your head off if you heard it, too, Martial artist Hyuk.
Apparently, Young Master Jin caught a dragon in Dongting Lake.”
“That’s definitely a rumor.
It was more of an imugi than a dragon.”
“Thought so.
I paid a thousand gold pieces for that information, and this is the kind of ridiculous...”
Hong Jin stopped mid-sentence.
After a breathless silence, he finally managed to squeeze out a few words.
“What did you just say?”
“Huh?
What do you mean?”
“No, just now.
You said it wasn’t a dragon...”
“Oh.
An imugi.
That’s right.
I was there, too.
At first I thought I was dreaming, but after a while I realized I wasn’t.
Well, it didn’t fly through the sky, so it definitely wasn’t a dragon.
It was an imugi.”
“By the way, what piece of shit leaked that information?
That was supposed to have been handled quietly, under the strictest secrecy.”
Still reeling as if time had stopped, Hong Jin realized that everything Hyuk Mujin had said earlier had been true.
Every last word.
Choosing Jin Taekyung really had been a stroke of genius.
An imugi?
He caught an imugi?
A person caught an imugi?
Wait, those things actually exist?
The shock was so great that, for a moment, he even forgot to worry about the young prince.
Just as Hong Jin stood frozen with his mouth hanging open, Hyuk Mujin, who’d been cursing the rumor-monger for some time, cautiously spoke up.
“Um, would you be willing to spend another thousand gold pieces?
I saw a talking tiger when I went to Nanman recently...”
“Move!”
A shout rang out, carried on internal energy.
It was a voice Hong Jin knew all too well.
Hong Jin whipped his head around.
His eyes widened like saucers when he saw who it was, while Hyuk Mujin, who’d been trying to strike a quiet deal, cried out on instinct.
“I’m sorry!
Please spare me!
I didn’t say anything!
May the Captain protect me—long live the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
“I’m back.
I have something to tell you, so let’s get inside...
Hyuk Mujin, you little shit, what’s wrong with you?
Why is he acting like that?”
Hong Jin had been about to tell him about the talking tiger, but his heart sank.
Where is His Highness...?
No matter how many times he looked around, he couldn’t see him.
His young lord.
The Great Nation’s last hope.
Hong Jin rubbed his eyes with his sleeve again and again, but only one person was coming toward him.
Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
So it’s come to this.
Something had definitely happened.
That cruel Emperor’s hand had finally reached his lord.
But Hong Jin fought back the haze gathering before his eyes.
It wasn’t over yet.
Surely that young martial artist had found some way out.
And as if to answer Hong Jin’s hopes, Jin Taekyung—who’d nearly knocked the Embroidered Uniform Guards, standing firm as iron towers, flying with a shoulder-check—moved his lips.
“Get inside the pavilion.
Right now!”
Of course, he didn’t forget to smack his one loyal subordinate on the back of the head in the moment he had to spare.
“Glad you returned safely...”
Whack!
“Ow!”
“Yeah, I’m back safe and sound, you little shit.”
Back at the pavilion, I used my internal energy to soundproof the place, then quickly laid out what had happened.
As briefly as possible.
Just the essentials.
First.
The Emperor had locked Prince Shangshan inside Qianqing Palace under the pretext of protecting him.
Second.
That Emperor was shameless as hell.
Like the rabbit in the old folktale who left his liver behind, he seemed to keep his conscience hidden somewhere else.
Oh, and he was a Supreme Peak master who looked way older than he was.
Third.
It seemed like the beloved concubine the Emperor had taken from the City Lord of Sichuan Province a few months ago was in Qianqing Palace.
That wrapped up my summary.
Even the twenty-first-century summary junkies who treated their eyes and scroll wheels as mere decorations would’ve given it a passing grade.
Hong Jin’s expression had changed with every point; now all that remained was unconcealable shock.
“The City Lord of Sichuan Province’s concubine... is staying in Qianqing Palace?”
“Yes.
Almost certainly.
But before I draw my own conclusions, there’s something I need to ask you.”
I took a deep breath and asked again.
“Is it normal for the Empress or the imperial consorts to stay in Qianqing Palace?”
“Not at all.”
“Even a consort the Emperor favors?”
“Not at all.
The rules of the imperial family are strict.”
“Then...”
“That’s right.
There’s only one explanation.”
Hong Jin and I met eyes.
The next moment, we spoke at the same time.
“Pregnant.”
“With child.”
Fuck.
The Emperor seemed to have found a new heir for the Great Nation to replace Prince Shangshan.

chapters.title: Chapter 877
paragraphs: It hadn’t made sense from the start.
These were members of the imperial family, not Chunshik’s family next door. Why would they all gather in Qianqing Palace and live together like one big happy family?
Besides, I’d been there. The place was closer to a fortress or a labyrinth than the Emperor’s living quarters.
Its passages twisted around like the Yeonsan Rotary in Busan. I wouldn’t have been particularly surprised to turn a corner and run into a Minotaur.
And that wasn’t all.
Assassins swarmed everywhere like Chinese cockroaches, and mechanisms and formations had been installed to deal with unwelcome visitors.
At that point, even the dungeon beneath the dormitory of some British school of magic would’ve looked like a five-star hotel.
But the Emperor couldn’t have created such a hopeless place simply because he was crazy.
He had a clear purpose.
Ironclad security.
That was why he’d stationed enough force there to stop any assassin from breaking through and filled Qianqing Palace with loyal servants he could trust.
And that security had held perfectly—until today, when some young ruffian fresh from Murim realized Aehyang was there.
Until he guessed one of the secrets the Emperor had tried hardest to keep.
Pregnant?
I felt as if someone had hit me in the back of the head with a sledgehammer. Across the table, Hong Jin and Hyuk Mujin looked just as stunned.
“Pregnant...? Is that true?”
“I can’t be certain yet, but it’s highly likely.”
Hong Jin answered Hyuk Mujin’s dazed question, then added quietly, “It would be best if all of this were utter nonsense.”
I nodded heavily.
To hell with family ties—the Emperor had seized the throne after practically bathing in his relatives’ blood.
If a child of his own blood were born under these circumstances, it was obvious what would soon happen to Prince Shangshan.
Pulling up the weeds by the roots.

The child who’d once had to leave the imperial palace in a rush, wrapped in swaddling cloth, had now grown into a proper young boy. And the seed of a towering tree, sprung from the same root, had taken hold and flourished.
That was more than enough reason for a suspicious Emperor to eliminate Prince Shangshan.
Clearing the line of succession.
Just as there couldn’t be two suns in the sky, there couldn’t be two Sons of Heaven.
The current Emperor ruled over the court and the people by suppressing their discontent, but he remained a tyrant and a traitor.
No, that legacy would pass to his new heir as surely as the blood in his veins.
Along with the label of a traitor’s child.

The powerful men holding back their resentment toward the Emperor wouldn’t welcome that. Those who’d drawn up the pledge—basically a rolling paper for signatures—already had an excellent alternative in Prince Shangshan.
And if Prince Shangshan disappeared, the Emperor couldn’t ask for a better outcome.
The air in the pavilion was heavy and cold, as if everyone were thinking the same thing I was.
Hong Jin had been staring into space, his gaze sunk deep, and a long silence had passed before he suddenly spoke.
“How did you guess?”
“What do you mean?”
“I know a fair amount about the imperial palace, but Young Master Jin couldn’t have made that guess just from knowing that a woman named Aehyang was staying in Qianqing Palace.”
I thought back to what had happened.
“I couldn’t have guessed from the sound alone. There was one other thing.”
“What was it?”
“The smell.”
“The smell?”
“Yes. It was faint, but I could clearly smell medicinal herbs. More precisely, a decoction.”
“A decoction...”

“To be honest, I do have people around me who know a lot about that sort of thing, but I don’t know exactly which herbs were used or what went into it. Still, when I thought about it, I could work out the general answer.”
I went on slowly.

“People take decoctions when they’re sick or need to build up their strength. So why would the Emperor be giving Aehyang one now? Was she simply ill, and he was worried about her? Or was there another reason?”
Fit all the circumstances and clues together, and a picture emerged.
This time was no different.
From what I’d seen, the Emperor was no lovesick romantic, and Qianqing Palace was no ordinary place.
“I could hardly believe it myself. That’s why I came back as quickly as I could.”
Hong Jin let out a low groan.
“How likely do you think it is, Young Master Jin?”
“Do you want the cold, hard answer?”
“Yes. The cold, hard answer.”
“At least ninety percent.”
“I’m sorry. But everything fits together too perfectly, as far as I can tell.”
It was a damnable reality, but I had to acknowledge it.
Why had the Emperor, after leaving Prince Shangshan alone for over a decade, suddenly summoned him to the imperial capital? Why had he all but forced him to stay in Qianqing Palace?
And... why might he want to harm him?
One answer resolved every question.
A new heir.
Hong Jin couldn’t have missed it, either.
No, he was probably more certain than anyone.
Even Ma Sanbao, who’d visited the night before, hadn’t said a word about something this important. The Emperor had kept Aehyang’s condition secret even from the East Depot.
Hong Jin, who’d held a fairly high position within the East Depot, couldn’t fail to understand what that meant.
Call it a guess, but read it as certainty.
The Emperor’s seed was growing inside Aehyang. It was all but a foregone conclusion.
He just doesn’t want to believe it.
I muttered to myself and watched Hong Jin in silence. Then I brought up one of the questions that still hadn’t been answered.
“I know this isn’t the best time, but may I ask you something?”
Hong Jin’s voice was subdued. “Anything.”
“Why didn’t the Emperor eliminate Prince Shangshan sooner? I mean...”
“Why didn’t he kill him?”
I nodded silently, and Hong Jin continued.
“I can’t know exactly what was in the Emperor’s heart, but one thing is certain. He was probably afraid of the backlash if he killed even a young prince who hadn’t been weaned yet.”
“Hadn’t he already killed countless people?”
“The purge didn’t happen overnight. Especially not the purge of the imperial family.”
“Tell me more.”

“Right after the Fourth Prince’s rebellion succeeded, the late Emperor and the other members of the direct imperial family were confined under strict surveillance. Then, over the course of a year, they died one after another, as if they’d arranged it among themselves. Strange, isn’t it?”
His voice was calm, but he couldn’t hide the shock and fear that lingered beneath it.
With a trembling hand, Hong Jin drew a long-stemmed tobacco pipe from inside his robe and lit it.
Hoo.
He took a deep breath and exhaled a pale plume of smoke.
For a moment, I thought I’d smelled it somewhere before. Then I turned my attention back to his story.

“I mobilized the East Depot’s full strength to rescue the late Emperor and the other royals, but every attempt failed. Everything I did was already being watched. It wouldn’t have surprised me if they’d thrown me in prison the very next day.”
“But the Emperor didn’t kill you.”
“That’s right. Maybe it was our old ties, or maybe it was a whim. Either way, the Fourth Prince let me live.”
“Old ties?”

“I spent decades in the imperial palace. I served the late Emperor closely, so I crossed paths with the Fourth Prince often enough. He was a talented, sharp-minded boy in many ways. At least back then.”
Hong Jin watched the smoke drift toward the ceiling, his gaze empty.

“In any case, I survived. I was finally allowed to see the late Emperor shortly before he passed away. His mind was clouded, almost as if he’d gone mad, but he still entrusted Prince Shangshan to me.”
“Wait. Gone mad?”
“Yes. But why would that—oh.”
Hong Jin realized what I was getting at. Confusion crossed his face.
“Surely not?”
“It’s possible. What exactly were his symptoms?”
“I saw him for less than fifteen minutes, so it’s hard to say. He’d been healthy enough to father a child at his age, but he was old.”
“I know. The rebellion and confinement must have been a terrible shock. But I need you to tell me exactly what you saw. That’s the only way...”
“We can see whether it was like what happened to the City Lord of Sichuan Province?”
Hyuk Mujin, who’d been listening with a dry swallow, widened his eyes. I nodded quietly.
Two words came to mind—Dark Heaven—along with the cursed creature I’d seen only about two weeks ago.
Blood Soul Gu.
A venomous creature that even Sichuan’s most renowned physicians had failed to detect.
It left almost no trace as it drove its host to death. Created centuries ago by the Five Poisons Sect of Nanman, it had been found in the corpse of the City Lord of Sichuan Province.
And the City Lord of Sichuan Province started showing strange symptoms months ago, on his way back from the imperial capital.
Could it really be a coincidence?
Hong Jin’s face had gone so rigid that I thought I could find the answer there.
“How likely do you think it is?”
After a silence, Hong Jin answered.
“Ten percent. No... twenty.”
“Do you know how the other royals confined back then died?”
“It was never made public. They were simply forgotten.”
“Then...”
“I’m going to contact Eunuch Ma tonight at the latest. His Highness’s life... may be in immediate danger.”
Right.

If the Emperor had planted Blood Soul Gu in the City Lord of Sichuan Province a few months ago and in the late Emperor more than a decade ago—or if Dark Heaven had done it with his help—Prince Shangshan was as good as dead.
But...
“I entrusted His Highness with a precious artifact I’d been carrying. We don’t need to worry too much right away.”
The Myriad-Poison Ring.
The Sichuan Tang Clan’s divine artifact had detoxified the Formless Ultimate Poison that had brought down even Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King, though he’d suffered a serious injury.
Blood Soul Gu was, in the end, a venomous creature created by the Five Poisons Sect. It couldn’t be beyond the Myriad-Poison Ring’s power.
No. It had to work.
“And one more thing. There’s something I’d like to ask Eunuch Ma to do for me personally.”
Hong Jin’s eyes widened at what I said next.
Hangzhou, in Zhejiang Province, had been one of the finest cities in the world for pleasure-seekers even before the imperial court moved there.
It had countless historic sights and beautiful views. Vast quantities of goods and wealth moved along its canals, and its brightly lit streets bustled with people late into the night.
A city that never slept, in every sense.
So there was nothing unusual about a customer arriving late at one of the many shops lining the imperial capital’s main road.
The employee’s attitude toward him was a little unusual, though.
“Go on, take a look around. If you like anything, ask me then.”
The middle-aged employee looked bored to death, his manner dripping with brusqueness. The customer studied him for a moment, then parted his lips.
“I’ve brought a message from the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
Beneath a sign that read Hyuk Family Textile Shop, the middle-aged employee—no, Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King—opened his eyes wide.

chapters.title: Chapter 878
paragraphs: The moment he heard the Sound Transmission, Jeok Cheongang moved with remarkable speed—and made it look perfectly natural.
“Oh, you’re looking for the finest Shu brocade? You should’ve said so earlier. Come on in.”
“No, wait. I was only...”
The man disguised as a customer tried to protest, but the terrifying qi flowing through Jeok Cheongang’s grip on his wrist left him gaping.
“Gah.”
The pressure felt as though it would crush his entire body.
He instinctively summoned his internal energy to protect his wrist. It did no good.
No—when he saw the flames pouring from Jeok Cheongang’s eyes, even the last scrap of his will crumbled to ash.
What the hell is with that look...
This wasn’t a man. He was a born beast of prey. A predator.
Frozen stiff against his will, the man was dragged deep into the textile shop.
Between towering stacks of cotton cloth and silk, two figures emerged like ghosts from a shadowy corner.
Thud.
In the faint lamplight, the faces of two young men, both around thirty, came into view.
One wore an expression as dry as if he’d been chewing sand. The other was handsome, but his sharply upturned eyes made him look almost sly.
Neither had the sort of face that made dealing with people easy.
The especially grim-looking young man spoke first, in a painfully awkward tone.
“Hey, Mr. Jeok. What’s going on?”
Jeok Cheongang answered, “Hey, Mr. Jeok? Are you that eager to shit blood?”
“...Oh. Not right now?”
“Can’t you tell by looking? How did you survive as a wandering martial artist with that little sense?”
“I’m sorry.”
The grim-looking young man bowed his head. Song Ilseom spoke again, more carefully this time.
“May I ask who that man is?”
“A customer.”
Jeok Cheongang gave the brief reply, then added, “But he used Sound Transmission. Mentioned a sobriquet that starts with ‘Blazing’ and ends with ‘Dragon.’”
Song Ilseom replied at once. “I’ll close up for today.”
“Make sure the shop is secured. Oh, first, circle the area. If you see anyone suspicious, grab the bastard and bring him here too.”
“Yes. But if I have no choice...?”
“What the hell are you asking me for? In that situation, slit his throat first.”
“Understood.”
“Just clean up after yourself. Make sure no one notices.”
“Leave it to me.”
Song Ilseom bowed politely and left at once. The man who’d heard their conversation felt his knees go weak.
Is this a textile shop or a slaughterhouse?
Could they be... an assassin organization?
Nothing in his orders had mentioned anything like this.
As his mouth went dry, the other young man spoke up.
“What should I do?”
“Bring the rest here. Every last one of them.”
“It’ll be difficult to bring everyone right away. One of them is out.”
“Damn it, what kind of goddamn idiot can’t sit still for a minute?”
“Well, it’s Young Lady Ju.”
“She’s allowed to go out for a while. Right. Of course. She must’ve gone to check on the situation nearby. How thoughtful of her.”
“Quit looking at me like that and go fetch the other freeloaders.”
“Yes.”
“Hey.”
“Yes?”
Jeok Cheongang stopped the young man as he was turning away and frowned.
“I told you not to look at me like that. Do my words sound like bullshit to you?”
“My eyes have looked this way since I was a child, so there’s nothing I can do about—no. I’m sorry. If I get the chance someday, I’ll be reborn.”
“Good. That way you can reincarnate. Maybe you’ll have kinder-looking eyes next time.”
Sama Pyo, the young man cursed with sorrowfully upturned eyes, left with a feeble reply. Jeok Cheongang suddenly reached toward something.
Swish.
Qi stretched out, invisible, and the air around them trembled.
So did the man’s pupils as he watched a wooden chest float through the air toward them.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space!

The man belonged to a rather extraordinary organization himself, so this wasn’t the first time he’d seen the technique. But he knew even a skilled internal-energy master would have to concentrate to pull in a chest that heavy.
Yet the middle-aged man before him had done it with ease.
With one casual wave of his hand.
Could it be...?
A possibility occurred to him, and he spoke cautiously.
“Could your sobriquet be the Fire King?”
Instead of answering, Jeok Cheongang blinked at him as if he were some curious creature. Then he kicked the man in the shin as fast as a flash.
Crack!
“Gah!”
“You little shit! You’re still wet behind the ears, and half your tongue seems to be missing. What was that—‘you’?”
“W-wait! Wait! Hear me out! I...”
“Stay right where you are. Move and you’ll get hurt worse.”
Thwack! Thwack! Thwack!
The grappling technique he’d practiced until his arms were bruised and the footwork technique he’d drilled until his leg muscles screamed were useless now.
After blows to the shin, stomach, chest, and finally the bridge of his nose, the man collapsed like a kite with its string cut.
Thump.
Of course, he wasn’t even allowed to pass out.
“Up.”
He sprang to his feet far faster than he’d fallen. His voice trembled as he spoke.
“Are you Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King?”
His tone could not have been more respectful.
Jeok Cheongang had perched on the chest he’d drawn over with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space. He looked as satisfied as a surgeon who’d just completed a difficult operation.
“Your severed tongue has finally grown back in the right place. Yes, this old man is Jeok Cheongang. And who are you?”
“This humble servant...”
“I don’t need to know a nobody like you’s name. Just tell me who you work for. I can tell at a glance you’re an eunuch, anyway.”
“What? Was that such a big secret?”
The man—or rather, the eunuch—was momentarily speechless. Jeok Cheongang gave a short laugh and continued.
“I’ll admit, you’ve put together a convincing disguise. That human-skin mask, even the beard—they look like they’re yours. But that’s not enough to fool this old man.”
“Then how did you...?”

“I felt your pulse earlier. You didn’t have nearly enough yang qi for a man. Now, tell me—which is more likely in the imperial palace courtyard: running into a eunuch, or running into a martial artist without balls? I don’t need to spell it out, do I?”
The eunuch swallowed hard. Jeok Cheongang’s judgment was sharp, but what unsettled him more was that knowing he was a eunuch hadn’t changed the man’s attitude at all.
“Then you must know where I came from, too.”
“Of course. The only place in the world with the perverse hobby of ripping the balls off perfectly healthy men is the imperial palace.”

“Stop rambling and answer what I asked. Exactly where in the imperial palace do you serve? Are you under that eunuch who’s Prince Shangshan’s right hand? The East Depot? Or are you one of the ones licking the Emperor’s...”
“The East Depot.”
“The East Depot, eh? The place where they gather the most stubborn and vicious eunuchs under heaven. So why has one of you come all the way here?”
“The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—no, your Disciple asked me to pass on several messages.”
“And the Emperor isn’t laying a trap?”
“Absolutely not. Your Disciple was the one who told us you were staying here.”
“That sounds plausible. But with the East Depot’s intelligence network, it wouldn’t be strange if you’d found out some other way. How will you prove it?”
As Jeok Cheongang’s eyes narrowed, the eunuch hurried to answer.
“M-Mong-su-ta.”
“What?”
“Your Disciple told me to say it. I have no idea what it means, but he said if I passed it on, I’d at least avoid shitting blood...”
The eunuch waited in dread. Fortunately, Jeok Cheongang knew exactly what the clumsily pronounced word meant.
Monster.
The monsters from the other world that had stained the realm of immortals with blood.
And only two people under heaven knew about them: Jin Taekyung and himself.
“Hmm. He definitely sent you.”
“Y-yes.”
“If you’d said that sooner, I wouldn’t have had to hit you. Forgive this old man’s rudeness, my good castrate.”
The eunuch wanted to say that calling a eunuch a castrate was about as rude as it got, but he held his tongue.
If he ran his mouth again, he might really end up shitting blood.
His best course was to leave as quickly as possible.
Swish.
He reached deep into his robes, took out a small tube, and handed it over. Jeok Cheongang’s eyes grew serious.
“Is this the missive Jin Taekyung told you to deliver?”
“Yes.”
“And the other one?”
As Jeok Cheongang had said, there were two tightly sealed tubes. The eunuch spoke in a low voice.
“The person I serve ordered me to deliver this one.”
“The person you serve?”
“You seem to know the Deputy Military Commissioner of Shanxi Province.”
“Hong Jin? I’ve never met him, but I heard about him on the way here. A fairly decent eunuch, apparently.”
“...Yes. The person I serve is close to him. He said the contents would help with what you’re going to do.”
“Is that all? Nothing else to tell me?”
“That’s all. I’m only a messenger.”
That was the extent of the eunuch’s orders.
He hurried out of the vast slaughterhouse—or rather, the textile shop—using a footwork technique. Left alone, Jeok Cheongang broke the seals and drew out two rolled-up missives.
Rustle.
The smell of oil-treated paper mingled with the stale air inside the shop.

Jin Taekyung’s missive opened with the immortal line “Looks like we’re screwed.” Jeok Cheongang read it, then quickly went through the information prepared with the East Depot’s help. He let out a quiet sigh.
“What a goddamn mess.”
And then—
Fwoosh.
Flames from Samadhi True Fire swallowed both missives, writhing in the darkness.
As Jeok Cheongang silently watched the missives turn to ash and vanish with a soft rustle in the blink of an eye—
“I brought everyone.”
Sama Pyo, who’d left only moments ago, approached with some familiar faces, then stopped short.
“Where is that man?”
“I sent him away a little while ago. Fortunately, he wasn’t suspicious.”
“Did you find out who he was?”
“An eunuch. One Jin Taekyung sent.”
“...What?”
Jeok Cheongang ignored Sama Pyo’s confusion at that painfully brief explanation.
“Where the hell were those people? What took you so long to bring them?”
Yaaawn.
Sama Pyo nudged Taishan in the side as he yawned, his eyes still sleepy, then hesitated.
“Well, you see...”
“Holed up in a corner sleeping, were they?”
“I think they dozed off for a bit.”
“Tell him next time he’ll sleep forever.”
“Yes.”
“What about Namho?”
Sama Pyo glanced at the old man, Namho, who was panting in rumpled clothes, and answered.
“He was choking Taishan.”
“Why?”
“Taishan drank all the liquor Elder Namho had hidden away.”
For a brief, tempting moment, Jeok Cheongang imagined choking Taishan and Namho at the same time. Then he sighed deeply.
“Quit screwing around and get ready, all of you.”
“Pardon me, but what should we...”
“We’re going to the imperial palace soon.”
“What? How?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes gleamed as he answered.
“Don’t worry. We’ve been formally invited.”

chapters.title: Chapter 879
paragraphs: Where there are people, there are rumors.
Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province—the heart of the world and the new imperial capital of the Great Nation—was no exception.
If anything, it was one of the worst places for them.
Wherever you went in Hangzhou, you found people repeating rumors they’d heard from someone else as if they were facts, spittle flying as they talked.

They discussed the beauty of a high official’s new concubine—the sort of official said to be powerful enough to knock a bird from the sky. They grew furious over the story that he’d squeezed the people dry to buy her expensive jewelry. And when they heard the Embroidered Uniform Guard had begun investigating, they raised their cups again and again.

“Times like this, there’s no one more dependable than the Embroidered Uniform Guard. He may have committed crimes against his own family to take the throne, but at least he knows how to get things done...”
“Shh. Shut that reckless mouth of yours. Didn’t you say one of that old official’s sons was in the Embroidered Uniform Guard?”
“I did.”
“And he still got caught? Even with connections in the Guard?”
“Oh, that one. Apparently, he was dismissed not long ago.”
“Really? Why?”
“Don’t know. Maybe he was on some secret assignment. He disappeared about a month ago, then came back a few days ago with his face all swollen.”
“Swollen?”
“Yeah. Looks like he got a real beating for something he did wrong.”
The story drifted away as quickly as it had come.
Poets and scholars seeking inspiration among scenic landmarks. Idlers who’d traveled a thousand li to visit Hangzhou, the city of pleasure.
Poor scholars quietly sipping cheap strong liquor over a plate of dumplings, and wealthy merchants patting their bulging bellies.
Hangzhou was full of all kinds of people, and they talked freely about what they’d seen and heard.
“I’ve finally seen West Lake. I could die right now without a single regret. If I had my way, I’d stay in Hangzhou for another year.”
“You’ve still got more than a month before you have to go home. What’s the rush? Let’s take our time looking around, then visit the Zhoushan Archipelago before we leave.”
“The Zhoushan Archipelago? Are you thinking of going to Mount Putuo?”
“That’s right. I don’t believe in Buddha, but if a famous mountain like that is nearby, I might as well visit while I’m here.”
“But I heard the nuns there are practically martial artists...”

“If you mean the Buddhist nuns at Putuo Temple, there’s no need to worry. They disappeared more than ten years ago, when the imperial capital moved here and Hangzhou’s martial artists were driven out.”
The poets and scholars who’d come to see Hangzhou’s famous sights were in fairly high spirits. The merchants seated nearby, on the other hand, kept pouring down liquor with sour expressions.
“Things are looking bad in Sichuan these days. Prices are swinging so wildly they’re impossible to predict. I’ve taken quite a hit.”
“Then is that rumor true? That foreign forces are about to pour in from Qinghai? They say even the Kunlun Sect, based in Qinghai, is on the brink.”

“Foreign forces? They’re nothing but lawless thugs from the martial world—fanatics thoroughly bewitched by demons, at that. They’ve given themselves a fancy new name, but they’ll still get smashed by the Central Plains sects, just like the Demonic Cult did in the past. The Imperial Guards won’t even need to get involved this time.”
“You’ve been in Hangzhou too long these past few years. You don’t know the first thing about what’s happening in the world.”
“Oh? Have you heard something?”
“A martial artist I’ve known for a long time is with the Murim Alliance now... He says this is far worse than when the Demonic Cult invaded.”
“What? That bad?”

“Just look at what happened in Sichuan a few months ago. Nearly ten thousand troops gathered and fought a bloody battle. At that scale, you can hardly call it an internal dispute within the martial world. It’s practically a war between small nations.”
“And that’s not all. Nothing’s been confirmed yet, but there are signs of some kind of movement in Yunnan, too.”
“Yunnan? You don’t mean those Nanman barbarians?”
“That’s right. They say the Nanman Beast Palace is mobilizing all its forces and marching north into the Central Plains. If the rumor’s true, they may have already reached Sichuan or Guangxi.”
“Hah. The fanatics weren’t enough, and now the barbarians are eyeing the Central Plains too?”
“No, it’s the complete opposite. They’re joining the Murim Alliance to fight Dark Heaven. But something about it is strange.”
“If that’s true, shouldn’t we be glad? What’s strange about it?”
“Well... I heard those barbarians are fanatics too.”
“What?”
“Apparently they spend all day spouting weird nonsense about how fighting Dark Heaven is a holy war, and how the Earth Mother Goddess watches over them.”
“What kind of fucking nonsense is that?”
“How should I know? I only heard it through my connections, several people down the line. Anyway, it’s clear something much bigger is happening than anyone thinks.”
The continent was vast. But merchants, whose line of work forced them to keep their ears open, heard all kinds of information through all kinds of channels.
Whether a rumor was true or not, it was worth remembering. Someday, it might make them a fortune.
Just as the inn had grown noisy with conversation and clinking cups, someone tossed out a slurred remark.
“Oh, have you heard? They say His Highness, Prince Shangshan, is staying in the imperial palace.”
In an instant, the air that had been warm with drink went cold.
Silence fell over the inn. Every gaze turned toward the same place.
“Huh?”
Startled by all the eyes suddenly fixed on him, the thoroughly drunk middle-aged man stammered.
“W-Why is everyone looking at me?”
Then a few people in the now-quiet inn spoke up.
“What did you just say?”
“His Highness, Prince Shangshan, is staying in the imperial palace? Not in Shanxi Province, his fief?”
“Are you sure about what you just said?”
Disaster always came from liquor and loose tongues.
As the questions came flying at him, the middle-aged man realized something was wrong. He sobered up all at once.
“I-I don’t know if it’s true. I only heard it somewhere. It’s probably just a rumor.”
“Even if it’s a rumor, tell us. Everything you know.”
“No, no. I must’ve said something foolish because I’m drunk. I need to leave now, so please let me through...”
His flushed face had long since turned pale.
Though he managed to stagger to his feet, he couldn’t take a single step. Something dropped from above and stopped him in his tracks.
Thud.
It landed right in front of his feet with a solid thump. The leather cord around its opening came loose, spilling the contents.
Clatter.
Silver nyang spilled from the money pouch, glinting in the dim light.
At a glance, there were more than thirty.
As people gaped at the enormous sum, a quiet voice reached their ears.
“That was quite an interesting story.”
Everyone turned again. No—looked up.
On the second floor, a young scholar sat alone at a table, watching the middle-aged man.
“Fifty silver nyang. I’d say that’s enough for the story. What do you think?”
The middle-aged man’s eyelid twitched.
He was stunned by the sum of fifty silver nyang—and by the young scholar who’d tossed it down so casually.
Enough?
It was more than enough. Far more.
Fifty silver nyang.
As a day laborer on Hangzhou’s canals, he’d never even dreamed of touching so much money. Just looking at it made his heart pound.
But the possible consequences of the words he’d tossed out so carelessly weighed on him as heavily as that pouch.
“W-Who are you, sir? You look like you come from a good family. Did I say something I shouldn’t have...?”
“There’s no need to worry. I’m simply curious.”
Fifty silver nyang just to satisfy his curiosity?
That was ridiculous.
Even a rich young master wouldn’t throw away that kind of money for no reason.
