It was an instinct honed through countless real battles and brushes with death—so subtle that I wouldn’t have noticed it if I hadn’t reached my current realm.
They’re not ordinary laborers.
I couldn’t sense any internal energy from them, but one thing gave them away.
The stench of blood.
It was like a brand no amount of washing could remove.
The sour smell of sweat and the mustiness of old clothes couldn’t quite cover it.
Martial artists?
Were they martial artists who’d voluntarily taken Energy-Dispersing Poison to hide their internal energy?
Or was it just my imagination, brought on by the fact that I had to be sensitive to everything happening around me right now?
I’ll know if I check.
I started toward them for a closer look—or tried to.
A cart, unable to bear its load, tipped toward me.
Crack.
Crash!
Wooden splinters flew.
Silver yuanbao and all kinds of ornaments spilled from the boxes, and the official clutched his head.
“What the hell do you think you’re doing?”
“I-I’m sorry.
I loaded the cart wrong, and...”
“You stupid old fool!
Forget apologizing and pick it all up!
If even one thing is damaged, you’ll pay dearly!”
“Yes, sir.
Right away.”
An old man bowed so low he looked ready to snap as the official stormed off.
Small and gaunt as a tree that had lost all its life, he limped over and looked up at me with frightened eyes.
“Are you all right, sir?
This old man’s mistake didn’t hurt you, did it...?”
A mistake.
Sure.
“I’m fine.
Not a scratch.”
“Phew.
Thank goodness.”
“It gave me a fright, though.
That cart looked perfectly sound before it suddenly fell over.”
He saw my smile and bowed again, flustered.
“I apologize once more, sir.”
“Don’t worry about it.
Want some help?
Looks like there’s a lot to pick up.”
“Oh, how could I ask that of you?
It’s more than I deserve that someone of your standing would speak so politely to me...”
“I’m not someone of high standing.
You know that already, don’t you?”
For an instant, something shifted among the laborers coming over to clear the mess.
In a pause too brief for anyone else to notice, the old man slowly opened his mouth.
“If you’d help us, we’d be very grateful.”
“Then that’s settled.”
I nodded, crouched down, and began gathering the scattered goods.
I worked in silence as though picking them up had been my only intention, but I kept my eyes on the old man.
He broke the silence first.
“How did you know?”
I let out a quiet laugh at the admission.
“You gave that up fast.”
“I hate wasting time.
Especially when I’m an old man without much of it left.”
“Are you a martial artist?
Who do you belong to?”
“Answering a question with a question is rude.
Remember that.”
“What does that—oh.”
“How did you know?
I was sure no one would notice.”
His eyes gleamed now, the frightened laborer gone as if he’d never existed.
“The stench of blood,” I said.
He didn’t look surprised.
He frowned, sniffed at various parts of himself, and smacked his lips.
“My nose must be failing with age.
All I smell is old-man stink.”
“That’s there too.
Since you brought it up, could we put a little distance between us?
I’m having trouble breathing.”
“I thought you were just skilled in martial arts, but you’ve got a hell of a nose, too.”
“You know me?”
“Of course.
Information is essential in this line of work.
But even without being told about you, I’d have known right away.”
“How?”
The stench of blood.
That shut me up.
The old man went on.
“Didn’t you know?
You reek of it yourself.
Enough that no one would blink if they called you a Killing Ghost instead of a Divine Dragon.”
“No need to look at me like that.
I mean it as a compliment.
You know what they say.”
He grinned, releasing a terrible stench from between his blackened, yellow teeth.
“Kill a hundred and you’re a Killing Ghost.
Kill a thousand and they call you a hero.
Kill ten thousand and you become... a king.”
My mouth felt gritty, like I’d been chewing sand.
I stared at the old man, whose breath stank right in my face.
What the hell is this?
Something about him felt wrong.
Just facing him sent a chill down my spine.
Even in Murim, with every sort of person roaming it, you rarely came across someone like this.
“Who are you?
No—who are all of you?”
“You address a Senior of Murim as ‘you’?
Does your master know his Disciple has such poor manners?”
“Someone I met recently told me it was rude to answer a question with a question.”
The old man stared at me, eyes wide, then burst out laughing.
“Well, you got me there.”
“Finished laughing?
Then answer me.”
“Why ask when you already know?
Those children and I are martial artists.
Not so different from you.”
“I’d say you’re very different.
Am I imagining it?”
“There’s no need to worry.
We may not belong to the Murim Alliance, but we’re in the same boat.”
“What does that...”
I trailed off as a thought struck me.
“No way...”
“Eunuch Ma.
Is that answer enough?”
“Everyone has their own place and role.
Go back and wait for the right moment.
Any more attention will only make things troublesome.”
The old man rose and bowed to me.
“We can manage the rest, sir.
You needn’t trouble yourself any longer.”
It was a clear dismissal—and a performance for whoever might be watching us.
No, calling it a performance almost did him a disservice.
He was an old laborer, every movement perfectly in character.
“Please get back safely, sir.
Then this old servant will be off...”
Step.
Step.
I watched him limp away carrying a box, and at last I thought I knew what the people disguised as laborers were.
Even in all of Murim, only a few sorts of people could hide themselves and move about so completely.
Add that stubborn stench of blood, and only one word came to mind.
Assassins.
Even martial artists, surrounded as they were by lunatics and people with no sense of self-preservation, had certain sorts they preferred to avoid.
The same few always made the list.
Killing Ghosts.
Fiends.
Mysterious old men.
Beautiful women in veils.
Like Japan’s legendary first-string team, they weren’t easy to find.
But martial artists with a shred of sense and dreams of retiring to a village for the elderly someday knew to steer clear.
Why?
Simple.
Even messing with them—and sometimes just being near them—made a sense of doom creep over you.
And right up there with Killing Ghosts and fiends, among the three most avoided professions, were assassins.
The three kings of utter bastards.
Nobody argued with the list.
Plenty of people even put assassins at the top.
Someone close to me had once given me much the same advice.
His sobriquet was the Slaughter Saint, which made it a little ironic.
Actually, that’s well past ironic.
It’s practically black comedy.
I kept walking as I muttered to myself.
It suddenly occurred to me that I didn’t know where this road led.
But that thought was quickly buried by the conversation with the Slaughter Saint that came to mind.
“A Killing Ghost or a fiend would be better.
But whatever you do, stay away from assassins.”
“Why?
Aren’t they all the same kind of lunatic?”
“Your head is a solid lump of rock, so let me give you a simple example.
Say you’re eating at an inn and a Killing Ghost or fiend suddenly walks in.
What do you do?”
“That’d be fucking awful.
I’m trying to eat.”
“Well... you’re not wrong.
But think a little harder before answering.”
“You just called me a blockhead.
I don’t want to think.
Can’t you tell me?”
“In case you’ve forgotten, I can break rocks with my fist.
A head made of stone is no exception.”
“I spoke too soon.
May I have a moment to think?”
“You’ve gotten a little smarter.”
“Thank you.
Hmm.
First, I’d watch the Killing Ghost or fiend, then carefully...”
“Yes.
Your first priority is to carefully get out of there.”
“No.
I’d hit them first.”
“...What the hell did the Fire King teach you?”
The Slaughter Saint had looked up at the sky and sighed.
Then he’d hit me on the head a couple of times with that rock-breaking fist before continuing.
“To put it more simply, Killing Ghosts and fiends are no different from madmen who don’t think about the consequences.”
“Ow, my head.
Doesn’t that make them more dangerous?
Like you said, if I met one at an inn, the whole place could turn into a sea of blood.”
“But you’d still have a good chance of surviving.”
“Well, sure, if your martial skill is high enough...”
“It has nothing to do with skill.
You can never predict people like that.
They kill or spare people on a whim.”
“They really are crazy.”
“But what about an assassin?”
“An assassin...
Oh.”
“Now you’re beginning to understand.
They aren’t merely madmen.
They’ll do anything to kill their target.
That’s how an assassin can kill a master a level or two above them.”
“They’ll do anything to assassinate their target...”
“That’s why you must be most wary of assassins and keep your distance.
Understood?”
“Yes.
Understood.”
“They’ve lost their place in the world, so you won’t find many these days.
Still... what are you doing?”
“Packing my things.”
“Why?”
“You told me to stay away from assassins.”
“Oh.
Does that not include former assassins?”
Man, I got beaten up a lot that day.
Then again, that was why I remembered the advice so clearly.
And now I’d run into those very assassins in the middle of the imperial palace.
If Ma Sanbao was going to bring in martial artists, why bring assassins into the imperial palace?
Just as a question I couldn’t answer right away rose in my mind—
“Stop.”
A clear, bright voice pierced my ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 886
paragraphs: “Stop.”
The clear, bright voice was the last thing I expected to hear. Instinct surged ahead of thought and took over my body.
Whoosh.
I blurred into motion, closing the three-zhang gap in an instant. My hand shot out, obeying instinct.
Toward the owner of that voice.
Toward her snow-white neck.
Whoom.
The wind, unable to keep up with my speed, arrived a beat late. With a heavy whoosh, her hair fluttered.
At the last moment, I fought down my instincts and stopped my hand in midair. I stared at the familiar face before me.
“What is it?”
“That’s what I’d like to ask you.”
So Gyo glanced at my hand, halted just in front of her throat.
“Striking out of nowhere like that. You’re as rash as you look.”
“I think you mean more rash than I look.”
“No, I think I had it right. Now, when do you plan to move that menacing hand?”
“When I’m sure.”
“Sure of what?”
Instead of answering, I sent the internal energy I’d drawn up spreading in every direction.
The System update had sealed my Skills, but that didn’t mean I’d lost the Qi Sense that was part of me as a martial artist.
Whoooosh.
The air rippled like water. I swept a radius of thirty or so zhang in an instant. Finding no one else nearby, I slowly lowered my hand.
Only then did my heartbeat begin to settle.
If this had been a trap...
Shit.
I’d let my guard down. Lost in thought, I hadn’t even noticed someone nearby. If I’d walked into a trap, I’d have had no excuse.
More importantly... why is she here?
As far as I knew, So Gyo was one of the Emperor’s people and stayed in Qianqing Palace.
For a moment, I wondered if I’d wandered deep into the Inner Palace without realizing it. I shook my head.
Impossible.

The boundary between the Outer Palace and Inner Palace was like the difference between heaven and earth. No matter how much freedom I’d been given to move around, I couldn’t have entered the Inner Palace unless every member of the Embroidered Uniform Guard protecting it had taken a group nap like golden retrievers at doggy daycare.
And even lost in thought, I couldn’t have passed all those people in the Inner Palace without noticing them.
Then I’m still in the Outer Palace. Was there a place like this inside the imperial palace?
I looked around.
Exotic flowers and rare plants crowded the grounds. Beside them lay a moss-covered pond, and at the center of it all stood a huge pavilion, rising like a mountain.
For all its size, the place felt desolate. There wasn’t another soul in sight besides So Gyo.
“Where are we?”
I hadn’t expected her to answer, but she proved me wrong.
“Forbidden ground.”
“Forbidden?”
“A place in the imperial palace no one wants to enter, and everyone keeps quiet about.”
“Two people have entered it already.”
“Do you not know the difference between won’t and can’t?”
“Oh.”
“This place was abandoned long ago. No one tries to come near it, so there’s no one to guard it.”
“Not even against outsiders like me?”
“Only thoroughly vetted people can enter the imperial palace. Even an outsider who doesn’t know this place exists wouldn’t stray this far if he had the slightest bit of common sense.”
“So you’re saying I’m an idiot with no common sense?”
“Thank you for saying it yourself.”
She got me there.
But thanks to what she’d said earlier, I thought I could guess where I’d wandered by chance.
“Does the reason no one comes here have something to do with what happened a little over ten years ago?”
“Your face tells me I’m right.”
So Gyo’s expression, composed until now, shifted ever so slightly. She regarded me with surprise, then gave a small nod.
“You’re more perceptive than you look.”
“This time, I think you meant as perceptive as I look.”
“I said it right. Just like a moment ago.”
Rather than snap back, I took another look at the desolate grounds.
So this is the place.
Something had seemed wrong from the moment I saw it. There was no one around, and the grounds had been neglected to an almost shocking degree.
But now I understood, at least somewhat.
If this was where the late Emperor and his direct descendants had been confined after the rebellion more than ten years ago, no one in the imperial palace would dare come near it.
But...
“Why are you here?”

That part made no sense. Why would So Gyo, one of the Emperor’s loyal followers, come to a place that was practically his sorest point? And why had she answered my questions so readily when I was all but her enemy?
“Don’t tell me...”
“I didn’t follow you. I thought we’d meet again soon, but I never expected it to be here.”
“Then why are you here?”
“Why should I tell you?”
“Well...”
I was at a loss for words and could only smack my lips. Then So Gyo, who had been watching me with composed eyes, suddenly spoke.
“Answer one question honestly, and I might tell you.”
“What?”
“I promise.”
What the hell was this woman after?
I thought it over for a moment, but I didn’t hesitate long. There was something I really wanted to know.
“In exchange, can I ask you something else?”
“Of course.”
I still couldn’t read what lay behind her calm expression. I frowned at her, then let out a small sigh.
“Let’s hear your question first. What do you want to know?”
“It’s simple.”
Her next words left me even more confused than before.
“How long have you been learning martial arts?”
“What...?”
“I mean exactly what I said. I asked when you started learning martial arts.”
For a moment, all I could do was blink.

Her question was so far from anything I’d expected that I’d been keeping my expression in check for nothing. I’d been prepared for something like How deep are you in with Ma Sanbao? Instead, the tension drained out of me, leaving only bewilderment.
“No, why would you suddenly ask that...?”
“Have you already forgotten our conversation a moment ago? You only need to answer honestly.”
She had a point.
I could tell her the truth. I had no idea why she wanted to know, but the answer couldn’t hurt me or any of my allies.
The problem was...
Who’d believe me?
I’d spent my time going back and forth between Murim and the modern world. Even adding the time I’d spent in both worlds together, it came to barely two years.
Who would believe I’d reached my current realm in just two years?
Even the handful of people who knew the truth hadn’t fully believed it. They’d simply let it pass, thinking there must be some circumstances behind it.
Even Jeok Cheongang, who’d watched me more closely and for longer than anyone else.
He didn’t fully accept it until he learned about the System and the modern world.
The idea that a Third Rate punk steeped in pleasure had become a Supreme Peak master who shook the Central Plains in only two years was simply beyond the bounds of what anyone could accept.
That was why rumors nowhere near the truth had become accepted as fact.
—Jin Taekyung is a secret weapon the Jin Family of Taiyuan raised at the cost of the family’s survival.
—They had him pretend to be a layabout from an early age so he wouldn’t catch the eye of the Mount Heng Sword Sect or the Head Elder.
—They funneled money to him under the pretense of paying a pleasure house. God knows how many elixirs they bought him with it. Jin Taekyung has three legs, they say.
That last one was a little strange, but anyway.

Rumors like that hadn’t sprung up for no reason. Becoming a Supreme Peak master in two years was impossible even if the heavens split in two, so the wild stories had quickly hardened into accepted fact. That suited me.
If I told the truth outright, I could be branded an irredeemable practitioner of demonic, heterodox arts—or worse, an enemy of all Murim who’d mastered terrifying demonic martial arts.
And if I tell So Gyo the truth, she won’t believe me anyway.
As far as I could tell, she was a First Rate martial artist herself.
Sometimes what looks true matters more than the whole truth.
Like now.
“Fifteen years.”
I met So Gyo’s eyes without a flicker of change in my expression.

“The story going around is that I caught a tiger with a pinecone when I was one, and learned the art of shrinking space when I was two... but that’s a load of bullshit only idiots believe. Going by the memories I still have, it’s been about fifteen years.”
So Gyo murmured, “Fifteen years.”
“You might not know this, but I have a brother just a few years older than me. I trained hard while he knocked me around. I had talent, too, of course.”
“Like Cheongpung, the Huashan Divine Dragon?”
“Right. Cheongpung—wait. You know him? Even his title?”
“I know far more than you think. I’ve kept up with news from Murim.”
“No, I mean, why would you need to?”
“There’s someone I need to find. Someone I absolutely must find.”
So Gyo answered calmly and turned away.
Or rather, she was about to when I shot out an arm as fast as lightning.
“I answered, so you need to keep your promise—”
And then—
Swish. Rustle.
A breeze passed between us.
“Huh?”
I stood frozen like a statue, staring dumbly at the hem of her robe as it brushed past my fingertips.
What was that?
I hadn’t used my full strength, but I’d moved more than fast enough to catch a First Rate martial artist.
Yet So Gyo had slipped past my hand with a movement technique so smooth she seemed to glide. As though it were the most natural thing in the world.
Was that just my imagination? Or...
A thought took shape in my mind, and the blood in my body seemed to turn cold. I glared at So Gyo, my eyes sinking deep.
“I didn’t know you could do that.”
“I can do quite a few things. Just as you can see.”
“Your movement technique is definitely beyond First Rate... Are you good at lying, getting under people’s skin, and running off, too?”
“Lying? I don’t think you’re in a position to accuse me of that.”
“What?”
“You said you’ve been learning martial arts for fifteen years. Every word of it was a lie.”
“Don’t underestimate the imperial family’s intelligence network. That’s why I’m staying here, too.”
A chill ran down my spine.
Her calm eyes seemed to pierce straight through me. And I had a feeling So Gyo wasn’t merely one of the Emperor’s loyal followers.
“You... what are you, exactly?”
Ssshhh.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi heated the air around me.

As though it were the most natural thing in the world.
Was that just my imagination?
Or...
A thought took shape in my mind, and the blood in my body seemed to turn cold.
I glared at So Gyo, my eyes sinking deep.
“I didn’t know you could do that.”
“I can do quite a few things.
Just as you can see.”
“Your movement technique is definitely beyond First Rate...
Are you good at lying, getting under people’s skin, and running off, too?”
“Lying?
I don’t think you’re in a position to accuse me of that.”
“What?”
“You said you’ve been learning martial arts for fifteen years.
Every word of it was a lie.”
“Don’t underestimate the imperial family’s intelligence network.
That’s why I’m staying here, too.”
A chill ran down my spine.
Her calm eyes seemed to pierce straight through me.
And I had a feeling So Gyo wasn’t merely one of the Emperor’s loyal followers.
“You... what are you, exactly?”
Ssshhh.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi heated the air around me.

chapters.title: Chapter 887
paragraphs: Sssshhh.
Heat like molten lava surged through countless acupoints, setting them ablaze.
I glared at So Gyo with burning eyes. My voice came out dry as ash.
“You... what the hell are you?”
“That’s quite a reaction. You should calm down and settle your internal energy before you overdo it.”
So Gyo—or rather, the woman whose identity I no longer knew—answered with her usual composure. But she’d dropped the polite speech and courteous manner she’d used to keep up appearances.
Then her next words hit me like a surging tide.
“Especially considering the state you’re in right now. Don’t you think?”
Was this what it felt like to have lightning strike through the top of your head?
My voice trembled before I could stop it.
“H-How?”
“Your internal energy isn’t flowing steadily.”
Her answer was short, simple, and impossible to argue with.
But that wasn’t why I’d lost my words. For her to give such an obvious answer, one thing had to be true.
Qi Sense.
Exceptionally keen Qi Sense, sharp as a blade.

Every fight began with gauging your opponent. A master could see how much internal energy a lesser martial artist possessed and what condition it was in, but the lesser martial artist couldn’t accurately gauge the master’s level.
And right now, I was unmistakably the latter.
A master!
There was no doubt. So Gyo was an incredible master.
A Supreme Peak master who’d reached the realm of Returning to Simplicity—able to hide herself so perfectly that even I couldn’t see through her.
So that movement earlier wasn’t a fluke.
I suppressed the sigh threatening to escape and quietly clenched my fists.
I had no weapon worth mentioning, and my body was in rough shape. No matter how optimistically I looked at it, I was in no condition to face a master a level above me.
Still, I lowered my stance at an angle and drew up my internal energy again.
“Who are you?”
So Gyo answered calmly.
“I have no obligation to tell you. You were the one who broke your promise and lied first, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
“Shut the fuck up and answer me. Whose orders are you following? The Emperor’s? Or...”
I glared at her and spat out two words.
“Lord of Heaven?”
“Who knows.”
A brief silence followed. So Gyo studied me with an expression I couldn’t read, then spoke again.
“If you knew who I was, what would that change?”
“It would change things. Lives are at stake.”
“Lives...”
“Yeah. Depending on your answer, someone here is definitely going to die.”
“If it comes to that, we already know who it’ll be. Don’t we?”
At that moment—
Sssshhh.
The air trembled. Her aura stirred the grass and flowers like a north wind, while her cold gaze and voice wrapped around me like winter frost.
But I didn’t waver.
I’d been through too many bloodbaths to fear someone just because she was strong—as a Hunter and as a martial artist of Murim.
“Yeah, maybe it’s already been decided to some extent. But who says only one of us has to die?”
“What?”
“I’ll kill you. No matter what.”
“I swear on everything I have. No—I guarantee it.”
My voice was so calm it surprised even me.
This wasn’t a desperate bluff from a weaker fighter backed into a corner. So Gyo could tell I meant every word.
“You... you’re serious?”
“Of course.”
“So you’re willing to die taking me with you. Ha.”
She gave a short, disbelieving laugh and looked me up and down like some strange animal.
“So the reports were true after all. I suppose you must have something up your sleeve to have survived this long.”

“The Blood Lord, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, and most recently, even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. The Sword Saint and the Fire King helped you through those crises, of course, but coming through encounters with all of them unharmed is nearly impossible.”
I stared at her, my gaze turning cold.
I had a feeling I no longer needed to hear the answer to my question.
She knows about the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
She didn’t sound as though she merely knew their names from reports. She spoke as if she knew what kind of people they were and how powerful they were—as if she’d met them before.
At last, I could see who stood behind the name and identity of So Gyo.
...Dark Heaven.
Yeah. What else could it be?
Hadn’t she said herself that one of the main reasons she stayed in the imperial palace was its vast intelligence network? She wasn’t a loyal servant of the Emperor. She had another purpose.
She meant to get the imperial palace—or rather, the Emperor—in her grip and pull the strings.
The scattered pieces of the puzzle fell into place.
The Fourth Prince’s sudden rebellion. The deaths of the late Emperor and the direct imperial family, and everything that had happened since.
But in the end, it had only been a partial success.

The Emperor had been replaced overnight, and countless people had gone to their deaths on the execution grounds. Even so, they’d failed to root out all opposition and take control of the entire Great Nation.
Then could it be...
Just as the last pieces were about to fall into place, So Gyo broke her silence.
“Let me ask you one thing. Why go this far?”
“Why?”
“Why fight me when your body’s in such poor shape? You’re even prepared to die taking me down.”
I was quiet for a moment. Not because I needed to think about my answer, but because it was so obvious to me.
“Because fewer of my people will die if I do.”
“What?”
“Even if we both die here, that’s better than letting a bitch like you live.”
“What if I said I had no intention of harming you?”
“That’s obviously bullshit, but sure.”
“Why?”
“Because a viper like you only does more harm the longer she lives.”
How many people had died already?
Every time Dark Heaven made a move, hundreds died. Then thousands. Eventually, tens of thousands vanished as lonely ghosts.
If my life was enough to put an end to that, I’d count myself lucky. Of course, the best outcome would be for me to live and So Gyo to die...
“But I don’t care either way. I won’t feel right until I’ve pulled out those damn fangs and stripped your skin off.”
This time, So Gyo fell silent. She kept her lips pressed together for a long while before tossing out a single remark.
“You’re even crazier than I thought.”
“What the hell are you talking about, you crazy bitch?”
“And I think I understand a little why Prince Shangshan, that child, looks up to you so much. Yes. I really do.”
“Are you threatening me because you’ve got a kid hostage?”
“Who knows?”
“What do you mean, ‘who knows’? Fuck. You’ve just given me one more reason to kill you, whatever it takes.”
“I like the enthusiasm. But things don’t always go the way you want.”
So Gyo shook her head slightly.
“To have reached this realm at your age... Your talent and what you’ve achieved are so remarkable they seem like a trick of heaven. No one could deny that. But...”
She went on slowly.
“Everything has its time. Being born with heavenly patterns won’t let you escape death.”
Swish.
I heard a faint sound against her collar.
The belt around So Gyo’s slender waist unfurled—no, it was a flexible sword. Filled with powerful internal energy, its blade pointed straight at me.
Beyond it, her eyes were cold.
“Shall we put it to the test? See whether heaven saves you or leaves you to die here?”
Whoooom.
A low, clear sword hum rang out.
Fwoosh.
Then I felt it unmistakably: an enormous, terrifying aura spreading from So Gyo, one I hadn’t sensed until now.
It closed around my whole body, pressing down on every part of me.
I drew in a breath without meaning to. The air had grown heavy in an instant, choking me. Every hair on my body stood on end, and cold sweat beaded on my skin.
But—
“Fuck off.”
I spat the words through my teeth and pushed against the invisible chains of internal energy. They bound my arms and legs tight, but I withstood them and moved toward So Gyo.
Crack. Thud.
One step.
Just one, and the solid bluestone beneath my foot shattered. The layers of earth below it caved in.
Was I that heavy? Had this place grown so decrepit after being abandoned for so long?
Neither.

I’d taken that step under the full pressure of internal energy weighing a thousand geun—ten thousand geun. And I’d withstood it not by countering her internal energy with my own, but with physical strength that had long since surpassed human limits.
Crunch. Craaack.
I put more force into my next step, trampling soil and flowers underfoot. Beneath them, I felt the bluestone fragments break again into dozens, then hundreds of pieces.
The closer I got, the stronger the pressure grew.
But...
I can take it.
A well-honed blade was a fine weapon on its own. So was the body I’d built by surviving countless brushes with death.
Strength. Stamina. Agility.
I excelled in all three. I’d surpassed my limits.
One of the main reasons I’d survived against enemies a level—or even two levels—above me was this body, which could wield superhuman strength without internal energy.
It could tear steel apart with bare hands, run for two days and nights without collapsing, and surge forward like the wind with a single push off the ground.
So even if several jiazi of internal energy closed around me, I could withstand it.
No. I could break it.
“Hah!”
With a short shout, I threw both arms out with all my strength.
Boom!
With so much power and speed behind it, the compressed air burst apart. I felt the internal energy that had surrounded and pressed down on me from every direction scatter.
Now!
My heavy body suddenly felt as light as a dandelion seed. I seized the opening and launched myself toward the one person staring at me with eyes now wide open.
So Gyo.
Fwoosh—boom!
Flamefire Path.
One step was all it took.

Scorching Yang Qi surged up from deep within my dantian and exploded from my foot. I crossed the five jang between us in an instant, blazing heat trailing behind me, and drove my fist forward like a cannon shot.
BANG!
The world shook.
Beyond the surging blue-white flames, a slender figure flew backward at tremendous speed to a roar that seemed to split the sky. Then she turned smoothly in midair.
Tap.
Her toes touched the blossom of a nameless flower, opened wide beneath the year’s strongest sunlight.
So Gyo landed on that single flower as lightly as a passing breeze. I almost gasped.
Ah.
Elusive, yet graceful.
Her movement technique was extraordinary. For an instant, I forgot she was my enemy. I even forgot I ought to press the attack while I had the chance.
So Gyo’s eyes flashed with something I couldn’t read.
“I couldn’t feel any internal energy from you at all... How did you do that?”
I wanted to ask her the same thing.
How had she blocked the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist I’d thrown with all my strength so easily? How had she met that blinding speed and force head-on without even looking strained?
You damn bitch. Have some conscience and at least pretend you’re struggling.
I grumbled to myself and gave a wry smile.
Why was I laughing now? I didn’t know. Maybe I really had gone crazy. Or maybe it was because I’d prepared myself to die before this fight began.
Yeah. That was it.
I’d been prepared for a long time.
“You die, I live.”
Laughing like a man half out of his mind, I took a step forward.
My condition?
Of course I wasn’t fine.
After unleashing so much power at once, my dantian was already lurching like an overworked engine. My internal energy no longer moved as freely as my hands and feet.
But this wasn’t a sport played in a ring. There was no referee to stop the match, no second to throw in the towel for a fighter in danger.
That was what a life-and-death duel meant. I’d known it all along.
I’d already made my choice.
My body might be failing, but my resolve didn’t waver.
Holding fast to that single thought, I charged So Gyo again.
Fwoosh!
The world slowed. The scenery around me shifted.
And at the moment I surrendered my whole body to the heat, the wind, and the fighting spirit bubbling like lava—
Screeeech!
With a violent whistle, a streak of light hurtled toward me like lightning.

chapters.title: Chapter 888
paragraphs: It all began and ended in the blink of an eye.
Whoosh!
A streak of light came hurtling in faster than the sound of it tearing through the air. And then...
KABOOM!
A deafening blast. A tremendous shock wave shoved my whole body backward.
“Hngh!”
Crack. I swallowed a breath and dug my feet in. The ground flipped up beneath them.
The gale whipped up by the impact sent pond water surging high into the air and swept through the rare flowers and plants covering the grounds.
Whooosh.
Anyone watching might have been overwhelmed for a moment and gasped in awe.
Countless petals swirling on the wind really were a spectacular sight.
But even the most carefree, clueless person would have groaned instead if they’d seen what had caused it.
Just like I was doing now.
“This is...”
My voice trailed off as I stared at it.
Amid the rain of pond water and petals, it stood embedded deep in the ground, radiating a chilling sharpness. I knew that weapon’s shape well.
“A crescent blade?”
The words slipped out before I could stop them. Then a low, resonant voice pierced my ear.
“Calling it just a crescent blade is a bit of an insult.”
I turned toward the voice. There was the face I’d half expected—and had very much hoped not to see here.
Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
I calmly addressed the man people called the Blood Envoy in fear.
“Then what is it?”
“Golden Dragon. That’s its name. It’s been my trusted weapon for over thirty years.”
“Golden Dragon, Goldie—doesn’t really matter to me either way. Still, I’m surprised.”
“Surprised by what?”
“Nothing. It just seems like if it’s your trusted weapon, Blood Dragon would suit it better than Golden Dragon.”
Baek Yeon had been approaching without hesitation, but at my pointed question, he stopped.
“Seems you’ve heard a few things about me.”
“Plenty. Sounds like Goldie had quite a feast about ten years ago. You killed a lot of people with it.”
“It’s Golden Dragon, not Goldie. And it was necessary.”
“Sure. I’m sure it was necessary.”
I glanced between So Gyo and Baek Yeon, speaking sarcastically.
“For reasons the rest of us haven’t been told.”
“Perhaps. I won’t bother defending myself, but even if only half of what you know or suspect is true, shouldn’t you be more careful about what you say and do?”
“Careful about what I say and do?”
I let out a hollow laugh.
“In a fucked-up situation like this, I’d cuss out the Emperor himself—or his grandpa. Don’t you think?”
I forced up the corners of my mouth, but I couldn’t do anything about the tightness in my chest.
I’d already been preparing to face So Gyo alone, ready to fight to the death. And now Baek Yeon had shown up, too.
I didn’t expect him to get here this fast. Was killing me already part of the plan?
Even calling this the worst possible situation didn’t do it justice. Heavy-hearted, I stepped forward and gripped the crescent blade a few paces away.
Shing.
It slid free, cutting through solid ground as easily as a knife through tofu. The blade gleamed silver, so clear it was almost transparent.
It felt strange in my hand because it belonged to someone else. Yet the sharpness was familiar, and the anger that had briefly settled in me surged back up.
“Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. Guess the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard gets a hell of a weapon. I’m borrowing Goldie.”
Baek Yeon stroked his chin beard.
“That’s a troubling offer.”
Why?
“Because you’ll try to cut her and me down with it.”
“Then you shouldn’t have thrown it over.”
“I was in a hurry. What else could I do?”
Baek Yeon shrugged.
“It has a deeper meaning to me, too. The late Emperor personally bestowed it on me the day I was appointed Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.”

“Then all the more reason I don’t care. The late Emperor would rather I used it anyway. If I said I was going to beat the traitorous bastards with it, he’d jump out of that pond and throw me Silverie, too.”
“And this isn’t an offer. I’m telling you.”
At that moment, I saw it.
I saw Baek Yeon’s thick eyebrows twitch, if only for a moment.
A brief silence fell. Then he spoke, his voice low and subdued.
“Must you really make such a fuss?”
“Will it end with just a fuss?”
I quietly went over the plan I’d revised while we talked.
If I fight them here, I’ll die for nothing. I need to draw as many eyes here as I can.
What would happen if I had to fight two masters who were both above me?
I didn’t need to think hard about it. I’d lose. No question.
I do have One Annihilation as a last resort, but I can’t even be sure that would work.
One Annihilation wasn’t invincible, and my body was already at its limit.
Even with the recovery I got from Level Ups, I’d ended up like this. What would happen now, without the System?
It really would be my last move.
The problem was, even if I burned my life away to use it, I might not take a single person with me. It could turn into a suicide mission that got me killed after missing my target.
That’s a little too far over the line.
I had no interest in becoming some dumbass who missed, exhausted himself, and died—or an SSS-rank suicide Hunter.
Now that things had come to this, I had no choice but to turn it into an all-out battle.
They had their own plans, and so did the anti-Emperor faction led by Ma Sanbao. But none of that mattered to me now.
No—the truth was, I didn’t have the luxury of thinking about their plans with those two monsters in front of me.
Since we’re here, I’ll pull every damn stunt I can.
Luckily, I had allies inside the imperial palace.
I didn’t know the details, but there were Murim assassins Ma Sanbao had brought in. And above all, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was there.
Not to mention the people already plotting against the Emperor.
We had a decent chance of winning that fight.
Now that I’d worked it out, there was no point hesitating. I angled the crescent blade in my hand, ready to get out of here at once.
Whooom.

They said a weapon that spent a long time with one owner could take on a soul of its own. As the blade trembled, seeming to reject its unfamiliar wielder and unfamiliar qi, I remembered something Jang Taebo had once said. The former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild was now a retainer of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
But...
Settle down.
Fwoosh.
Its brief resistance vanished as blue-white flames flared up, and I launched myself forward with all my strength.
Or I would have.
Just as the flames of Flamefire Path were about to burst from my feet, So Gyo spoke.
“You’d better stop before you regret it.”
“What?”
“Prince Shangshan. Zhu Bao.”
Just five syllables, but they were enough to stop me in my tracks.
In all the confusion, I’d overlooked one thing.
Right.
They still had that child.
As long as Prince Shangshan was in Qianqing Palace, the Emperor held his life in his hands.
Qianqing Palace was a demon-slaying battleground. Just from what I’d seen with my own eyes, there were no fewer than four Supreme Peak masters there, including the Emperor.
It wouldn’t matter if it were me or the Fire King. Even if the Martial God himself returned, he couldn’t do anything about the blade at the young prince’s throat.
“Choose which path to take. And think about what awaits you at the end of it.”
Her tone was calm. The air around us was cold, and I had to force my voice through clenched teeth.
“What the hell are you trying to get out of this?”
“You don’t need to know. What matters is that you’ll survive here today.”
Survive? Me?
The lackeys of Dark Heaven would just let me go, now that they had leverage over me?
I could only blink at her unexpected words. Then So Gyo added,
“And I hope you do.”
“You do?”
“Yes.”
“Because there’s still a reason to keep you alive. That’s my mission, too.”
My eyes widened before I knew it.
I’d heard something like that only a few months ago.
From none other than the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
That was why I couldn’t help seeing the Southern Heaven Demon Empress as she’d been then, overlaid with the So Gyo standing before me now.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress had held back from killing me as much as she could, even right up until she was about to turn into a monster. Just like So Gyo is now.
If so, the meaning could only be one thing.
Just like the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, So Gyo—or rather, the Lord of Heaven—still wanted me.
Not my cold corpse, my soul already gone.
Me.
Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
Why?
None of it made any sense. I’d thwarted Dark Heaven’s plans at every turn, even cutting off two of their limbs in the process: the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
The Lord of Heaven had begun a war with the Murim of the Central Plains. As far as he was concerned, I was one of the obstacles he ought to chew to pieces.
So why?
A memory flashed through my mind.
The underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan. The whispers of that deep darkness I’d briefly encountered when it borrowed the body of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, who had unmistakably died.
How interesting. How very interesting.
And the eerie laughter that had seeped through that darkness.
We’ll meet again.
Had it started then?
Had those words been the beginning?
Crack.
Without my noticing, I’d clenched my fist so tight it had gone white, the veins standing out across it. Every hair on my body stood on end as I tried to steady myself. So Gyo watched me calmly.
“So, what’s your answer?”
I closed my eyes, forgetting for a moment that I had an enemy right in front of me.
Then, the next instant—
Swish.
I reversed my grip on the crescent blade and hurled it like a beam of light.
Whoosh! Kaboom!
The blade tore through the air. A thunderous boom followed.
Baek Yeon recovered his weapon from where it had buried itself deep in the ground one step ahead of him and clicked his tongue.
“You have quite a dramatic way of returning it.”
If this had happened just fifteen minutes ago, I’d have fired back with a sarcastic quip. But not now.
I gritted my teeth and spoke to the two of them.
“Don’t... touch Prince Shangshan.”
“Rest assured. Nothing like what you’re worried about will happen.”
I had no way of knowing whether that answer was true or false.
All I could do was look for another way.
Still, I learned one thing. As long as the Lord of Heaven’s orders stand, they can’t move against me lightly.
Suppressing the killing intent I felt toward So Gyo and Baek Yeon, I started walking. To borrow a saying from Murim, from this moment on, fifteen minutes would feel like three autumns.
The grand banquet would soon be held in the imperial palace.
That celebration would become the battlefield where our fates were decided.
The Hongmen Banquet. So who’s Xiang Yu, and who’s Liu Bang?
I turned and walked away without hesitation. Before I’d completely disappeared from their sight, with my back to them, So Gyo’s voice suddenly reached me.
“Why did you give up fighting, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung? Do you want Prince Shangshan to become Emperor, too?”
A laugh escaped me.
The question hardly deserved an answer.
Still, I kept walking without turning around.
“Yeah. Since we’re going this far, of course I want him to become Emperor. But that’s not the only reason.”
“Then what is?”
“He’s a kid.”
I kept going, with no idea where I was headed, and muttered,
“He’s still a kid, you crazy bastards.”

chapters.title: Chapter 889
paragraphs: Those who were going to leave left. Those who were going to stay stayed.
So Gyo watched Jin Taekyung until he vanished in the distance, turning over the faint words the wind had carried to her moments ago.
He’s still a kid, you crazy bastards.
She wondered what expression Jin Taekyung had worn then, and how much of the anger and bitterness in his departing figure had been genuine.
There was no way for her to know.
You can plumb ten fathoms of water, but never one fathom of a person’s heart.
As So Gyo repeated the saying to herself, Baek Yeon spoke.
“How much of this did you intend?”
“Intend?”
“Did you intend for Jin Taekyung to come here?”
So Gyo shook her head slightly.
“Not particularly. What happened just now was a coincidence.”
“A coincidence. Then why did you ask His Majesty to let him move about freely?”
“I needed to watch him more closely. You already know some of the reasons I’ve been staying in the imperial palace, don’t you?”
“Could it be...?”
Baek Yeon’s eyes widened. So Gyo answered in an even voice.
“I can’t be certain yet...but I think he’s the one. The person I’ve been looking for. The person that person foretold.”
The beautiful woman in her thirties spoke to the graying veteran without the slightest formality, but Baek Yeon paid it no mind.
The woman calling herself So Gyo had the standing and the strength to speak that way. Besides, her answer was more astonishing than he’d expected.
“So that’s why you had him stay in the imperial palace?”
“I had to see for myself whether the rumors about the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung, were true. Whether he really was the one that person spoke of. And...”
So Gyo turned her head. Her gaze swept over the place where someone had been moments ago, though that person was already gone. For an instant, her eyes gleamed sharply.
“What kind of person he is.”
The chance encounter had turned out well. Perhaps not for Jin Taekyung, who had left in anger, but So Gyo had seen enough to sort out her thoughts and gain a measure of certainty.
The Huashan Divine Dragon, Cheongpung. The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
She placed the names of the two rising martial artists she’d been watching on the scales in her mind. Unlike when she’d first learned of them, the scales now tipped toward one.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
As she’d told Baek Yeon, it was too soon to be certain. But given Jin Taekyung’s past actions and what she’d seen and sensed herself, there was a good chance he was the person she sought.
That must be why that person entrusted this task to me.
So Gyo slowly crossed the flower garden.
Their brief clash had left it looking as though a storm had swept through. At its center, something that had been hidden beneath the flowers and grass poked up through the dirt.
“It’s been a long time.”
How deep had it been buried? How long had it lain there?
So Gyo greeted the familiar object as if speaking to herself, then reached out.
Whoooom—thunk!
An enormous, unseen surge of qi shook the air. Two objects buried deep in the ground shot up into So Gyo’s hands.
They were identical in length and width, as if measured with a ruler. Each curved gently toward its tip, much like a saber.
So Gyo hung one at each hip, then spoke to Baek Yeon, who was watching her.
“It’ll be a fierce battle. Maybe fiercer than the one over a decade ago.”
Baek Yeon nodded.
“I’m prepared.”
“Enough to stake your life on it?”
“Do you know something?”
His expression remained calm as he went on.
“I’ve always staked my life on getting what I wanted. That’s how I made it this far.”
“I hope you do the same this time.”
“I must. I will.”
Baek Yeon’s eyes grew as grave as his voice.
“May I ask you one thing?”
So Gyo nodded.
“Anything, if it’s something I can answer.”
“Why are you leaving the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung, alone?”
“Why?”
“That’s right.”
“You must have guessed already.”
“Of course I have. But before we wipe them all out in one place, we should go after Jin Taekyung right now—”
“Impossible.”
So Gyo cut him off firmly.
“There’s still more I need to confirm. Until then, it’s better to let things proceed as they are.”
“What if he becomes an obstacle to the great undertaking?”
“An obstacle? How?”

“As you know, Jin Taekyung’s master is the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. And, as it happens, he vanished without a trace after reaching the Imperial Capital. The other Murim martial artists following Jin Taekyung won’t make much difference, but...if they draw the Fire King in as well, things could become complicated.”
Baek Yeon was genuinely worried.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The government and Murim might be meant to stay out of each other’s affairs, but after more than a hundred years, there was no one in the land who hadn’t heard of him.
And Baek Yeon, who had led the Embroidered Uniform Guard since the late Emperor’s reign, knew better than most which of the countless rumors about the Fire King were true.
A hero born of the Great Faction War. A demon awakened by the Demonic Cult.
A man whose martial prowess towered above even those powerful enough to be called kings.

He could not reach someone born in a human body and called a god, but he stood shoulder to shoulder with the Three Stars. If he took the other side, they would have to be prepared for tremendous losses.
Even with So Gyo, Baek Yeon himself, the Emperor, and several other Supreme Peak masters on their side.
“Their forces are already formidable. And that’s only what we’ve managed to learn so far. If the Fire King joins them after Jin Taekyung...”
“The Fire King? That wouldn’t be bad.”
For a moment, Baek Yeon doubted his ears.
Then So Gyo continued, a faint smile on her lips, and he realized she meant it.
“No. That might be even better.”
Leaving Baek Yeon frozen like a statue, unable to understand her at all, So Gyo turned away with a quiet laugh.
The words she hadn’t told him drifted through her mind.
Wait. You’ll know soon enough.
Baek Yeon thought he knew everything, but he was wrong.
The story So Gyo had kept from him was something only she and the Emperor knew. Secrets were better off unknown.
At least until the banquet both allies and enemies were so eagerly awaiting.
“Only three days left until then.”
So Gyo looked up at the sky, now dark, and murmured. Cold raindrops began to fall, as if confirming her sense that the calm before the storm was already upon them.
Shaaah.
Heavy rain hammered everything around us.
It swallowed even the shouts of palace attendants running here and there in woven bamboo hats and rain cloaks.
I’d spent a good while in Murim, but I’d never seen a downpour like this. The unexpected rain and thunder were more than enough to obscure the watchers’ view.
“You’re really going?”
Hyuk Mujin’s face was tense.
“I have to.”
“What if they catch you...?”
“They won’t. Not in this situation. You were there and heard it too, so you know.”
“I know. I know it’s urgent. But still...”
“It’ll be all right if it’s Young Master Jin.”
Hong Jin spoke up, his voice subdued.
“Even if they spot him, there’s a good chance they’ll pretend they didn’t.”
“Huh? What do you mean?”
“If what Young Master Jin told us is true, they want to wipe us all out at once. They intend to uproot us in one fell swoop...and that leaves us no choice.”
I nodded silently.
Would So Gyo and Baek Yeon have let me go without thinking it through?
Even knowing full well I’d tell their enemies what had happened?
No way.
This was both a warning and a declaration: don’t try to avoid the all-or-nothing battle ahead. And we couldn’t refuse.
With Prince Shangshan in their grasp, there’s no way out of it, no matter what we do.
Our enemies had engineered this situation because they were confident they’d win. But however thoroughly they’d prepared, whatever traps they’d set, we couldn’t back down.
We have to fight. Right now, before we worry about winning or losing, we have to make a decision.
The stage was set. So were the actors.
Our enemies had built the stage intending to star in the show. But sometimes a supporting actor defies everyone’s expectations and outshines the lead.
That was my job.
To change who took center stage—and how this story ended.
Fortunately, there was one important cameo in the imperial palace that our enemies didn’t know about.
Old Master.
I stared out the window at the sheets of rain.
The downpour obscured my view, and the sky was already pitch-black. Below the pavilion, members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard stood watch in shifts.
There were about twenty of them, every one a Peak master.
But even Supreme Peak masters couldn’t predict a sudden lightning strike.
Flash! Kaboom!
Now.
At the instant white light flashed and a thunderous boom rang out, I pushed off the railing and sprang into the air.
Whoosh!
The Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, a signature martial art created by the greatest assassin of all time, unfolded beneath my feet.
I hadn’t been taught it formally; I’d only worked a little of it into my movements. But that was enough to slip past the watchers in the brief confusion.
Tap. Swish!
I landed on the roof of a pavilion whose name I didn’t know, one said to house the palace attendants, and shot forward—quietly but swiftly.
The layout of the imperial palace was already etched deep in my mind. I didn’t hesitate.
From here, along the east-west axis.
The grounds were vast, with pavilions scattered across them.
My black clothes blended into the darkness, and the guards posted throughout the grounds never caught sight of me.
“Damn, it’s really coming down.”
“The grand banquet’s right around the corner, and now the weather’s like this...”
The Imperial Guards grumbled as they looked up at the sky from beneath the eaves. They had no idea an uninvited guest had just passed two steps behind them and entered the Outer Palace.
But not everything went smoothly.
“What are you doing here?”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
“If I remember the regulations correctly, your assigned post isn’t beneath the eaves.”
The Imperial Guards weren’t the only ones startled by that voice, hard as rock. I was about to move on when I saw the familiar face that had suddenly appeared and swallowed a groan.
Fuck, what’s that bastard doing here?
Jeong Hogun.
A high-ranking Thousand Captain in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, he was walking toward the Imperial Guards.
And at the same time, he was heading toward me, concealed not far away in the darkness.

Those who were going to stay stayed.
So Gyo watched Jin Taekyung until he vanished in the distance, turning over the faint words the wind had carried to her moments ago.
He’s still a kid, you crazy bastards.
She wondered what expression Jin Taekyung had worn then, and how much of the anger and bitterness in his departing figure had been genuine.
There was no way for her to know.
You can plumb ten fathoms of water, but never one fathom of a person’s heart.
As So Gyo repeated the saying to herself, Baek Yeon spoke.
“How much of this did you intend?”
“Intend?”
“Did you intend for Jin Taekyung to come here?”
So Gyo shook her head slightly.
“Not particularly.
What happened just now was a coincidence.”
“A coincidence.
Then why did you ask His Majesty to let him move about freely?”
“I needed to watch him more closely.
You already know some of the reasons I’ve been staying in the imperial palace, don’t you?”
“Could it be...?”
Baek Yeon’s eyes widened.
So Gyo answered in an even voice.
“I can’t be certain yet...but I think he’s the one.
The person I’ve been looking for.
The person that person foretold.”
The beautiful woman in her thirties spoke to the graying veteran without the slightest formality, but Baek Yeon paid it no mind.
The woman calling herself So Gyo had the standing and the strength to speak that way.
Besides, her answer was more astonishing than he’d expected.
“So that’s why you had him stay in the imperial palace?”
“I had to see for myself whether the rumors about the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung, were true.
Whether he really was the one that person spoke of.
And...”
So Gyo turned her head.
Her gaze swept over the place where someone had been moments ago, though that person was already gone.
For an instant, her eyes gleamed sharply.
“What kind of person he is.”
The chance encounter had turned out well.
Perhaps not for Jin Taekyung, who had left in anger, but So Gyo had seen enough to sort out her thoughts and gain a measure of certainty.
The Huashan Divine Dragon, Cheongpung.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
She placed the names of the two rising martial artists she’d been watching on the scales in her mind.
Unlike when she’d first learned of them, the scales now tipped toward one.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
As she’d told Baek Yeon, it was too soon to be certain.
But given Jin Taekyung’s past actions and what she’d seen and sensed herself, there was a good chance he was the person she sought.
That must be why that person entrusted this task to me.
So Gyo slowly crossed the flower garden.
Their brief clash had left it looking as though a storm had swept through.
At its center, something that had been hidden beneath the flowers and grass poked up through the dirt.
“It’s been a long time.”
How deep had it been buried?
How long had it lain there?
So Gyo greeted the familiar object as if speaking to herself, then reached out.
Whoooom—thunk!
An enormous, unseen surge of qi shook the air.
Two objects buried deep in the ground shot up into So Gyo’s hands.
They were identical in length and width, as if measured with a ruler.
Each curved gently toward its tip, much like a saber.
So Gyo hung one at each hip, then spoke to Baek Yeon, who was watching her.
“It’ll be a fierce battle.
Maybe fiercer than the one over a decade ago.”
Baek Yeon nodded.
“I’m prepared.”
“Enough to stake your life on it?”
“Do you know something?”
His expression remained calm as he went on.
“I’ve always staked my life on getting what I wanted.
That’s how I made it this far.”
“I hope you do the same this time.”
“I must.
I will.”
Baek Yeon’s eyes grew as grave as his voice.
“May I ask you one thing?”
So Gyo nodded.
“Anything, if it’s something I can answer.”
“Why are you leaving the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung, alone?”
“Why?”
“That’s right.”
“You must have guessed already.”
“Of course I have.
But before we wipe them all out in one place, we should go after Jin Taekyung right now—”
“Impossible.”
So Gyo cut him off firmly.
“There’s still more I need to confirm.
Until then, it’s better to let things proceed as they are.”
“What if he becomes an obstacle to the great undertaking?”
“An obstacle?
How?”
“As you know, Jin Taekyung’s master is the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
And, as it happens, he vanished without a trace after reaching the Imperial Capital.
The other Murim martial artists following Jin Taekyung won’t make much difference, but...if they draw the Fire King in as well, things could become complicated.”
Baek Yeon was genuinely worried.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The government and Murim might be meant to stay out of each other’s affairs, but after more than a hundred years, there was no one in the land who hadn’t heard of him.
And Baek Yeon, who had led the Embroidered Uniform Guard since the late Emperor’s reign, knew better than most which of the countless rumors about the Fire King were true.
A hero born of the Great Faction War.
A demon awakened by the Demonic Cult.
A man whose martial prowess towered above even those powerful enough to be called kings.
He could not reach someone born in a human body and called a god, but he stood shoulder to shoulder with the Three Stars.
If he took the other side, they would have to be prepared for tremendous losses.
Even with So Gyo, Baek Yeon himself, the Emperor, and several other Supreme Peak masters on their side.
“Their forces are already formidable.
And that’s only what we’ve managed to learn so far.
If the Fire King joins them after Jin Taekyung...”
“The Fire King?
That wouldn’t be bad.”
For a moment, Baek Yeon doubted his ears.
Then So Gyo continued, a faint smile on her lips, and he realized she meant it.
“No.
That might be even better.”
Leaving Baek Yeon frozen like a statue, unable to understand her at all, So Gyo turned away with a quiet laugh.
The words she hadn’t told him drifted through her mind.
Wait.
You’ll know soon enough.
Baek Yeon thought he knew everything, but he was wrong.
The story So Gyo had kept from him was something only she and the Emperor knew.
Secrets were better off unknown.
At least until the banquet both allies and enemies were so eagerly awaiting.
“Only three days left until then.”
So Gyo looked up at the sky, now dark, and murmured.
Cold raindrops began to fall, as if confirming her sense that the calm before the storm was already upon them.
Shaaah.
Heavy rain hammered everything around us.
It swallowed even the shouts of palace attendants running here and there in woven bamboo hats and rain cloaks.
I’d spent a good while in Murim, but I’d never seen a downpour like this.
The unexpected rain and thunder were more than enough to obscure the watchers’ view.
“You’re really going?”
Hyuk Mujin’s face was tense.
“I have to.”
“What if they catch you...?”
“They won’t.
Not in this situation.
You were there and heard it too, so you know.”
“I know.
I know it’s urgent.
But still...”
“It’ll be all right if it’s Young Master Jin.”
Hong Jin spoke up, his voice subdued.
“Even if they spot him, there’s a good chance they’ll pretend they didn’t.”
“Huh?
What do you mean?”
“If what Young Master Jin told us is true, they want to wipe us all out at once.
They intend to uproot us in one fell swoop...and that leaves us no choice.”
I nodded silently.
Would So Gyo and Baek Yeon have let me go without thinking it through?
Even knowing full well I’d tell their enemies what had happened?
No way.
This was both a warning and a declaration: don’t try to avoid the all-or-nothing battle ahead.
And we couldn’t refuse.
With Prince Shangshan in their grasp, there’s no way out of it, no matter what we do.
Our enemies had engineered this situation because they were confident they’d win.
But however thoroughly they’d prepared, whatever traps they’d set, we couldn’t back down.
We have to fight.
Right now, before we worry about winning or losing, we have to make a decision.
The stage was set.
So were the actors.
Our enemies had built the stage intending to star in the show.
But sometimes a supporting actor defies everyone’s expectations and outshines the lead.
That was my job.
To change who took center stage—and how this story ended.
Fortunately, there was one important cameo in the imperial palace that our enemies didn’t know about.
Old Master.
I stared out the window at the sheets of rain.
The downpour obscured my view, and the sky was already pitch-black.
Below the pavilion, members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard stood watch in shifts.
There were about twenty of them, every one a Peak master.
But even Supreme Peak masters couldn’t predict a sudden lightning strike.
Flash!
Kaboom!
Now.
At the instant white light flashed and a thunderous boom rang out, I pushed off the railing and sprang into the air.
Whoosh!
The Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, a signature martial art created by the greatest assassin of all time, unfolded beneath my feet.
I hadn’t been taught it formally; I’d only worked a little of it into my movements.
But that was enough to slip past the watchers in the brief confusion.
Tap.
Swish!
I landed on the roof of a pavilion whose name I didn’t know, one said to house the palace attendants, and shot forward—quietly but swiftly.
The layout of the imperial palace was already etched deep in my mind.
I didn’t hesitate.
From here, along the east-west axis.
The grounds were vast, with pavilions scattered across them.
My black clothes blended into the darkness, and the guards posted throughout the grounds never caught sight of me.
“Damn, it’s really coming down.”
“The grand banquet’s right around the corner, and now the weather’s like this...”
The Imperial Guards grumbled as they looked up at the sky from beneath the eaves.
They had no idea an uninvited guest had just passed two steps behind them and entered the Outer Palace.
But not everything went smoothly.
“What are you doing here?”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
“If I remember the regulations correctly, your assigned post isn’t beneath the eaves.”
The Imperial Guards weren’t the only ones startled by that voice, hard as rock.
I was about to move on when I saw the familiar face that had suddenly appeared and swallowed a groan.
Fuck, what’s that bastard doing here?
Jeong Hogun.
A high-ranking Thousand Captain in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, he was walking toward the Imperial Guards.
And at the same time, he was heading toward me, concealed not far away in the darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 890
paragraphs: Clank. Clank.
Heavy footsteps drew closer, accompanied by the metallic clatter of heavy armor.
Hidden in the darkness just thirty feet away, I felt my heart seize up at Jeong Hogun’s sudden appearance.
What the hell are you doing here...?

I didn’t know why a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, which was responsible for the Inner Palace, had wandered all the way out here. But one thing was certain: at this distance, one clumsy move could give me away to Commander Jeong.
Damn it. If I’d known this would happen, I should’ve learned the concealment technique properly.
Regret washed over me, but it was far, far too late for that.

I’d struggled tooth and nail to survive in Murim, and that was how I’d met Jeok Cheongang. After inheriting the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy, a good old-fashioned brawl had become both my only major and my general-education requirement.
What kind of sect was the Fire Gate Clan?
Just look at the records of its past Sect Leaders. Every last one of them was a no-holds-barred tough guy. The kind of lunatic who looked like he’d take a shit standing up.

For three hundred years, this hipster sect with a pedigree had picked fights with the orthodox, unorthodox, and demonic paths alike. To the Fire Gate Clan, the concealment technique was practically a symbol of weakness.
One of its Sect Leaders, said to have been the greatest master in the world some two hundred years ago, had even left behind this record:
Want to learn the concealment technique? Then you’re a homosexual.
Behold the audacity of treating one of Murim’s essential survival skills as a martial art for fags.

If he’d said that in the twenty-first century, a mob would’ve beaten him with rainbow-colored clubs. But for better or worse, this was Murim, a world steeped in barbarism, and the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage had carried on.
The problem was that, thanks to those fine ancestors and their policies, I was about to get screwed.
Seriously, shit. In three hundred years, couldn’t one Sect Leader have learned the concealment technique?
My mouth went dry. Maybe it was nerves, but I was starting to need to piss.
Jeong Hogun had come within ten feet of me. His face was hard as he questioned the Imperial Guards who’d neglected their post.
“Answer me. Why did you leave your assigned post?”
“S-Sorry, sir. The rain was so heavy, we started shivering...”
“Would you say the same thing if traitors slipped into the imperial palace undetected?”
“Of course not. We’re truly sorry, but...”
“Enough excuses. Who is your immediate superior?”
“W-Well, that is...”
“You don’t want to say? No, judging by how you’ve neglected your duty, perhaps you don’t want to serve in the Imperial Guard at all.”
“N-No, sir!”
“Then is this inside or outside?”
What was this? It reminded me of the Hunter Training Center.
Is this bastard a System user...?
I kept my presence hidden as best I could and watched, entertaining that reasonable suspicion about Jeong Hogun. Then he said something that made me doubt my ears.

“As of today, you are no longer members of the Imperial Guard. Go to your superior immediately, report what happened here, and turn in your badges, uniforms, weapons, and other equipment. I’ll guard this post myself until your replacements arrive.”
It was a bolt from the blue.
For the guards who’d only taken shelter from the rain beneath the eaves—and for me, waiting desperately for Jeong Hogun to leave.
“G-General!”
“Military law is strict. This is an order from me as a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.”
No. Don’t listen to him.
You’re civilians now anyway. Just punch him.
I fervently cheered on the middle-aged reservists—I mean, the Imperial Guard soldiers—but the two men who’d just been sent through the process of discharge still had a shred of reason left.

In the military, when they tell you to jump, you ask how high. And the Embroidered Uniform Guard was the place that could even cut off the heads of the highest officials—the sort who could make a flying bird drop from the sky.
Only two kinds of people could tell Jeong Hogun to go to hell right now:
Lunatics. Or people hoping to join the Fire Gate Clan.
Unfortunately, the two men in front of him were neither. They were perfectly normal.
“We’ll... obey your order.”
Their voices weak, they pulled their rain hats low and trudged away.
Or they tried to.
Just as Jeong Hogun had a moment ago, someone entirely unexpected appeared.
“How strange. Since when could the Embroidered Uniform Guard dismiss Imperial Guards on a whim?”
Swish.
The hem of a long robe brushed a puddle. A figure emerged through the endless rain. Jeong Hogun was silent for a moment before speaking.
“Eunuch Ma, what brings you here?”
“Nothing in particular. I was taking care of something outside and am on my way back. But...”
Ma Sanbao—the East Depot’s second-in-command and its de facto leader—smiled faintly.
“Could I have an answer to my question, Commander Jeong?”
“...I was only enforcing military law.”
“Of course you were. I know what a fine and capable man you are. But...”
At that moment, Ma Sanbao’s voice, which had always seemed to hover somewhere between a man’s and a woman’s, dropped low.
“Follow procedure. Follow procedure.”
“That’s...”

“The Imperial Guard may be under the Embroidered Uniform Guard, but there’s still a process to follow, isn’t there? The authority to impose a final punishment clearly belongs to their superior. That’s the military law you mentioned.”
“That’s all I have to say. Is there anything else?”
Jeong Hogun stared at Ma Sanbao in silence, then spoke.
“No.”
“Good. Since we’ve run into each other, why don’t we walk together for a while?”
“Walk together?”
“Yes. It’s been quite some time, and I’m glad to see you. Besides, there’s something important I’d like to discuss. You’re heading back to the Inner Palace anyway, aren’t you?”
Jeong Hogun probably meant to answer, “No,” or “Now isn’t a good time.”
His expression didn’t change, but for an instant I could see his wariness and reluctance in his profile.
Ma Sanbao was half a beat faster.
“Oh, you don’t mind? Good. I knew you’d say that.”

The East Depot’s authority had been curtailed after the rebellion more than a decade ago, while the Embroidered Uniform Guard had risen to prominence. Even so, Ma Sanbao had long since become the East Depot’s de facto leader in place of the bedridden Cang Gong.
Before Jeong Hogun could get a word in, Ma Sanbao seized the initiative with an easy smile and patted him on the shoulder.
“Come along. There’s plenty to tell the Embroidered Uniform Guard—and plenty I need to hear.”
Ma Sanbao was both a Supreme Peak master and a skilled politician. For Jeong Hogun, a martial artist through and through, he was the worst possible opponent.

Having lost control of the conversation in an instant, Jeong Hogun could only leave with him, his face rigid as a rock. He did remember to leave a stern warning for the two Imperial Guards who’d escaped their surprise firing.
“As soon as your shift ends, report what happened here to your superior. Understood?”
“Y-Yes, sir.”
“Understood!”
Of course they’d say yes now.
The guards snapped to attention and gave a hearty salute. Jeong Hogun turned away, and I was breathing an inward sigh of relief when a Sound Transmission reached my ear.
—I don’t know exactly why you’ve come all the way here, but there are many eyes watching. Be careful and use your wits. I’ll send word to you myself later.
I whipped my head around. Ma Sanbao was looking my way and winking.
He knew. From the beginning.
I was a little startled, but it made sense when I thought about it.

Ma Sanbao was a master of the concealment technique who’d reached the Supreme Peak realm. He might not be as skilled as the Slaughter Saint, hailed as the greatest assassin of all time, but he was more than capable of spotting my amateurish attempt.
Did he expect me and come looking? Or was it just a coincidence?
I had no idea.
I didn’t know why he’d appeared here, or how he’d brought the assassins of Murim into this.
What mattered right now was that the Imperial Guards still nearby weren’t skilled enough to detect me.
Swish.
I moved like a shadow through the darkness, helped by the unrelenting rain and crashing thunder.
After leaping over several pavilions and walls, I picked up a timely hint from a conversation between some other Imperial Guard soldiers.
“Have you seen ‘that guy’?”
“Who? Oh, I think I know who you mean. He’s a monster.”
“I thought he was just big, but damn, can he eat. Especially five-spice pork. It hasn’t even been half a shichen, and he’s already put away more than twenty plates. The cooks are up in arms.”
“Good grief. I’d heard about him, but that much?”
“He’s a lunatic, I’m telling you. At this rate, they say he’ll eat every pig in Zhejiang Province with that mouth of his within a month. He looks like he’s got a pigsty in his stomach.”
“Impressive. But wouldn’t it be better to kick him out?”

“The imperial family has its reputation to consider. They can’t treat people brought here for the grand banquet poorly just because they eat a little pork. Orders have already been given to provide them with whatever they need for lodging and meals.”
“Good grief...”
They hadn’t even said his name. Just that guy.
Why was I embarrassed on his behalf?
Taishan, you bastard...
I looked to the heavens and sighed. Then I noticed a group hurrying somewhere.
There were a dozen or so of them, each carrying a large plate.
And then there was the rich smell of five-spice pork, strong enough to clear the nose of someone with sinusitis.
I’d known my companions were staying somewhere in the Outer Palace, but not where their rooms were. I hadn’t expected to find them this way.
Is this for real?
I followed the group like Hansel and Gretel, quiet enough that no one noticed me.
All the while, a middle-aged man who looked like a cook fired off curses in a steady stream.
“Please, just stop fucking eating. If you’re human, please...”
That was when I saw it.
The large kitchen knife in his other hand was trembling.
“Food’s here.”
Creak—BANG!
The door to the pavilion flew open with a rough shove, and the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was surprised twice.
First, the middle-aged cook, who clearly hadn’t learned martial arts, was giving off genuine killing intent.
Second, behind the exhausted cook and the others carrying stacks of food, a familiar face was peeking out of the darkness.
“What is it?”
“N-Nothing.”
“If it’s nothing, take some of this food. My arms are about to break.”
The cook’s reply was sharp. He had the palace attendants set down the plates, then left—after warning them that if they ordered five-spice pork one more time today, he’d poison it.
No sooner were they gone than a breeze blew open the door they’d just shut.
At least, that was how it would have looked to anyone else.
“What are you waiting for? Get in here.”
At the Fire King’s abrupt command, a young man appeared from the darkness and grinned.
“I’m here.”
